items.name: Console shell (ground, falloff, gutter, scroll frame)
items.purpose: The frame every manager screen sits in: one ground, one gutter line, one scroll behaviour.
items.anatomy: Full-bleed `ground` #0B1017. Letterbox falloff paints the top and bottom 96dp as a 4-stop LinearGradient ground → vignette #0F1620 → vignette → ground (4 stops, not 2, because 2 band on a 6-bit panel). One scroll column. Gutter s5 = 20 on phone, s8 = 40 at ≥1080 (`TiqSpace.gutterFor`). Top pad s6 = 24 below the status bar unless a plate is first, which runs full-bleed to the top edge and suppresses the falloff there. Bottom pad = navOcclusion 100 (16 inset + 64 pill + 20 safe offset) + s6 = 124. Block gap s6 = 24; intra-block s3 = 12. REVISED: the 40dp of deliberate nothing before a first section rule exists only at ≥600dp — on a phone it was a tablet gesture costing half a decision row. No card, no panel, no shadow; Panel is reserved for the AI answer, forms and sheets. Structural separation anywhere in the console is whitespace, never a sub-3:1 line.
items.states: Default. Scrolling: no chrome change, no scroll-listener fill swap, nav opaque always. Refreshing: a 2px `ink2` rule travels the top edge, 1400ms linear. Offline: the banner inserts as the first child under the rules in Offline / stale banner — never under an active pointer. Auth lost: hands off to Session ended.
items.behaviour: Pull-to-refresh on touch; an explicit 44dp labelled Refresh icon-button for mouse. Refresh invalidates every provider together so no two panels disagree. Route change: 320ms reveal, enterCurve, content translates 8dp up with opacity 0→1, 40ms stagger over the first four children only. REVISED: no count-up anywhere in the console — the reveal is the only entry motion, because counting a number that arrived at t=0 implies a second measurement and costs the exact frames a 2 GB device does not have. Skeleton at 0ms, travelling rule after 600ms.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: ground Palladian #EEE9DF, falloff to #E6E0D4, same geometry. Veld (manager outdoors = Veld × Field): pure white, no falloff, gutter s6 = 24, block gap s8 = 40, every hairline a 2px #1B2632 border, and the nav docks so the bottom pad falls to 72 + safe area.
items.accessibility: One scrollable, one semantics order, top to bottom. No horizontal page scroll at any width; only tables and wide charts get their own overflow box. At 2.0× gutters and block gaps hold; only row heights grow. Reduced motion: reveal and stagger instant, travelling rule static.
items.amber: None. The shell is the unlit room.
items.screenshot: A near-black phone screen, warm off-white type hanging off a left line 20dp in, the very top and bottom slightly deeper black than the middle so it reads as a lit space rather than a flat swatch. Nothing boxed, nothing centred.

items.name: The amber ledger (TiqLedger)
items.purpose: Moves the amber law out of the components and into the screen, so the default rendering is the legal one and the count is lintable.
items.anatomy: NEW, and the critique's most important structural fix. Every component that can emit light ships `lit: false` as its constructor default and renders its unlit form — `ink1`/`ink2` fill, marker and weight — with no knowledge of its neighbours. A `TiqLedger` InheritedWidget at each route's root holds one `litId` (nullable). A component asks `TiqLedger.of(context).isLit(myId)`. The nav pill's active slot is EXEMPT and is not an id in the ledger: it is persistent chrome, like the focus ring, and only one slot can be active at a time. Night budget is therefore nav block + exactly one content amber = two lit objects, as the law always said. Day and Veld: the nav is never amber, so their one amber block is the screen's commit.
items.states: Nominated (the screen names an id), unnominated (no content amber at all, which is the correct state of Alerts, Tasks, Reports, the fraud queue, the scorecard and every configuration list), and violated — two non-chrome ids lit on one route throws in debug and renders the second unlit in release.
items.behaviour: REVISED CONSEQUENCES, each of which deletes a substitution rule from an earlier draft: the filter rail's selected chip is never amber on any screen; the stat tile's amber target tick is deleted outright, because a target is an annotation, i.e. a label; the progress bar's threshold tick is `ink2` in a list and amber only on a single-contest detail that nominates it; the trend series and the ranked focus bar are amber only when nominated. Nothing's colour now depends on how many neighbours it has.
items.modes: Identical in all three skins; only the legal amber form changes (Night: rim, line, bloom, block. Day/Veld: one solid block, because Burning Flame on white is 1.79:1 and can never be a line, an icon, a border or a word).
items.accessibility: Nothing the ledger controls is the sole carrier of meaning: a lit object is also the one carrying a marker, a weight step and a word. A screen with no nomination loses no information.
items.amber: This item IS the amber count. One content object per screen, plus the exempt nav slot in Night.
items.screenshot: Not a visible component — but its effect is that the same ranked bar, dropped on two different screens, looks identical until a screen deliberately lights it.

items.name: Press and confirmation feedback
items.purpose: Makes a tap visibly land on a cheap panel at 40% brightness, so nobody double-taps an irreversible control.
items.anatomy: NEW. The critique is right that every press state was a 1.1–1.5:1 fill step. Night presses cannot invert (there is no darker ground), so a Night press earns a second channel: fill `lifted` #2C3B4D across the pressed bounds, PLUS a 3px `ink2` #C9C1B1 tick at the screen's leading edge running the pressed object's full height (10.67:1 on ground — it is the visible channel, the fill is support), PLUS scale 0.98, PLUS `HapticFeedback.selectionClick()`. The leading tick sits at x = 0, outside the gutter, so it can never be confused with the decision row's 3px severity bar at x = 20, which is crimson and 40dp tall.
items.states: Pressed, released, disabled (no press response at all, and `inkMute` ink — a disabled control must look disabled and must not appear to accept a tap), busy, and committed.
items.behaviour: A commit-class control enters its busy state on touch-UP, within one frame, before any network call — the confirmation is local and is never awaited. Optimistic list collapses begin on touch-up for the same reason. Commit presses take `HapticFeedback.mediumImpact`. The double-tap guard on Acknowledge stays, but it is now a belt, not the braces it used to be.
items.modes: Night as above. Day INVERTS by construction: `lifted` is #2C3B4D, an ink block on paper, so a pressed row goes dark with `ground` ink on it (9.43:1) — no tick needed, and the earlier spec's `well` press (1.14:1) is deleted. Veld inverts the same way to the #1B2632 block with white ink (15.33:1) and has no scale, since Veld runs `TiqMotion.off`; its feedback is the inversion plus the haptic.
items.accessibility: Press feedback is never the only confirmation of a state change — the record on screen changes too. Haptics are additive, never load-bearing. Reduced motion keeps fill, tick and haptic and drops the scale.
items.amber: None, except when the pressed object is itself the screen's one amber, which goes to `amberPressed` #F79742 with dark ink (8.59:1).
items.screenshot: A list row held down: it darkens slightly and a short pale vertical bar appears hard against the left edge of the screen, level with the row.

items.name: First-paint fold budget
items.purpose: Turns "what is visible before a scroll" from a vibe into arithmetic with a failing test.
items.anatomy: NEW, from the critique's blocker. Definitions: vh = viewport height minus the system top inset. navOcclusion = 100dp on phone (16 + 64 + 20), 72dp + safe area in Veld where the nav docks. plateHeight = min(clamp(0.44 × vh, 200, 360), vh − 440); if that is under 200 the plate does not render at all and the collapsed 96dp hero band replaces it. The Floor's below-plate chrome = s5 20 + filter rail 44 + s6 24 + section rule block 24 + s5 20 = 132. Visible list = vh − plate − 132 − navOcclusion, which the cap guarantees is ≥ 208dp: two decision rows at the revised 76dp min-height, their 12dp gap, and 32dp of the third — enough of a title to prove the list continues.
items.states: 360×640 (Samsung A04, the binding case): plate 200, visible list 208. 360×780: plate 340, visible list 208. 412×892: plate 360, visible list 300. At 2.0× text the plate goes to its 200 floor and the guarantee falls to one full row, which is the declared minimum. Veld: no plate, so the first row is 168dp from the top.
items.behaviour: Golden tests at 360×640, 360×780 and 412×892, each at 1.0× and 2.0×, assert the number of fully visible decision rows on The Floor and the number of visible stat cells on the territory view. A layout change that eats the fold fails CI rather than a review.
items.modes: The formula is skin-independent; Veld substitutes its own docked navOcclusion and drops the plate term.
items.accessibility: The rule exists because a screen whose purpose is "what is broken" must show something broken before a gesture. At 2.0× the plate yields first and the list last — nothing above the list is allowed to grow into it.
items.amber: None.
items.screenshot: Two phone frames side by side at 640 and 780dp tall: the photograph is visibly shorter on the small one, and both show the same two-and-a-bit decision rows above the floating nav.

items.name: Floating nav pill + primary circle (manager)
items.purpose: Four destinations and one primary action, floating above the content rather than welded to the edge.
items.anatomy: Two objects on one baseline, inset s4 = 16 each side, 20dp above the safe area. PILL: height 64, radius 14, `well` #141D27 fully opaque, 1px `edgeStructure` outline (3.73:1 on ground). Five slots — Floor, Work, Territory, Ask, Menu — equal flex cells, each a 24px 2px-stroke icon over an 11/700 label with s1 between; inactive ink `navInkInactive` #8AA0B8 (6.32:1 on well). ACTIVE slot: solid `flame600` block, radius 10, height 48, inset 8, ink `onAmber` #0B1017 (10.65:1), weight 700. CIRCLE: 56dp, s3 right of the pill, plus-over-clipboard glyph, `lifted` fill, 1px `edgeControl`, `ink1` glyph. Pill width = viewport − 32 − 56 − 12.
items.states: Active / inactive. Pressed per the press model. Circle default / circle-as-next-move (`flame600` fill, `onAmber` glyph) / pressed (`amberPressed`) / disabled (`well`, `inkMute`, explained by the screen, never by a tooltip). Badged: a 6px `bad` dot plus the count appended to the label ('Work 7'), so the dot is never the only signal. Under 360dp and at 2.0×: icon-only, labels gone, the active block keeps its solid fill. Offline: unchanged.
items.behaviour: REVISED: tapping the circle opens a two-item sheet (Raise a task / Assign a visit); it does not guess, and the second action is no longer behind a long-press nobody would find. Long-press does nothing anywhere in the console. REVISED: the active slot's amber is exempt from the ledger and therefore never disappears — the earlier route-dependent substitution would have read as the app losing its place, and the critique is right that no navigation behaves that way. The pill never hides or recolours on scroll: zero BackdropFilter, one opaque ColoredBox.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: active block is `lifted` #2C3B4D with `ground` ink (9.43:1) — Day spends its single amber on the screen's commit. Veld REVISED: the pill DOCKS — full-bleed to the bottom edge, 72dp, 2px #1B2632 top border, no float, no radius; active slot a solid #1B2632 block with white ink (15.33:1); circle 72dp with a 2px border. A white pill floating 20dp above white rows in glare stopped reading as a bar, and docking gives back 36dp of fold Veld needs.
items.accessibility: Each slot is `Semantics(button:, selected:)`; the amber block is never the only state cue (weight 700 and `selected` carry it). The circle's `semanticLabel` is a required non-null argument. Slots ≥ 44 × 56, circle 56 (72 in Veld).
items.amber: One — the active slot block, in Night only, and EXEMPT from the per-screen content budget as persistent chrome. Every Night screen therefore reads: nav block + at most one content amber.
items.screenshot: A dark rounded bar hovering just above the bottom of the screen with four small icons and one warm amber block glowing around the active icon, and a separate dark circle with an amber-free plus glyph floating to its right.

items.name: Menu sheet (nav overflow)
items.purpose: The destinations the four slots cannot hold, grouped by verb so a manager scans instead of reads.
items.anatomy: Bottom sheet, radius 14 top, `surface` #1B2632, 1px `edgeStructure`, grabber 40 × 4 `ink2` @40% centred 8dp down (the one centred object). Scrim @72%, no blur. Max height 80% of viewport, scrollable. Three groups in fixed order: OPERATE, INSIGHT, CONFIGURE, each an eyebrow at 11/700 with tracking REVISED to +4% and permission to wrap to two lines (Afrikaans group names at +8% uppercase clipped). Rows: min-height 44, 20px icon, s3, `title.m` 16/600 `ink1`, separated by 1px `hairline` inset to the gutter — legal here because the labels carry the meaning and the line is decorative. Current route: `raised` fill + a 3px `ink1` left bar + weight 700. REVISED: 'Assign a visit' is a real row in OPERATE, not only a circle action.
items.states: Default, pressed (`lifted` fill with the ink flipping to `ink1`), current, disabled-by-role (label `inkMute` with a `meta` reason beneath: 'Admin only'), search-filtered (a 44dp trough filters live; zero matches shows the console empty state inline, left-aligned). Never loading — the destination list is a const.
items.behaviour: Opens 320ms reveal from the bottom. Dismiss on scrim tap, drag past 40%, or back. Selecting a row closes the sheet (200ms exit) before routing, so the route change is not animating behind a closing sheet.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: `surface` #FAF7F2, 1px `edgeStructure` #857C6B, sh1, current row `raised` #F4F0E8, press inverts to the `lifted` ink block. Veld: white, radius 0, 2px border, rows 64dp, a flat 72% overlay rather than a scrim fade.
items.accessibility: `scopesRoute` named 'Menu'; focus moves to the first group heading on open and returns to the Menu slot on close. Group headings are `header: true`. Role-disabled rows stay in the tree and announce 'dimmed, admin only'.
items.amber: None. A navigation list is never emitted light.
items.screenshot: A dark panel risen from the bottom over a dimmed dashboard, three small uppercase group headings in warm grey, and a plain list of labelled icons with one row filled slightly lighter and marked by a short pale bar at its left.

items.name: Section rule (knocked-out label)
items.purpose: The console's only section marker — no eyebrow, no number, no emoji.
items.anatomy: A rule running gutter to gutter with the section's name sitting on it, left, at `title.m` 16/600 `ink1`, the rule knocked out 12dp either side of the text, baseline centred on the line. Rhythm: s8 = 40 above, s5 = 20 below (s6 = 24 above on phone where a plate precedes it, per the fold budget). Sentence case, never uppercase. REVISED: the rule is `hairline` #3A4B60 in Night (2.14:1 — visible on a dark ground, and the text carries the meaning) but `edgeStructure` #857C6B in Day (3.41:1), because Day's hairline at 1.18:1 is nothing and the section rule is now the console's only full-width line, so raising it inverts no hierarchy.
items.states: Default. With a count: the count follows the name in `figure.s` 16/600 tabular mono `ink3`, inside the same knock-out ('Needs a decision 5'). With an action: a ghost text action at the right end, 44dp tall, `label` 13/500 `ink2`, knocked out 12dp before it. Collapsed: a 16px chevron, the rule unbroken beneath. Empty section: rule and name still render, followed by one `body` `ink2` line — a section that vanishes when empty makes a manager think the feature is gone.
items.behaviour: Static unless it carries an action or a collapse. Collapse animates 200ms, stateCurve, persisted per session only — a manager who collapses 'Held' this morning should still be shown held work tomorrow.
items.modes: Night `hairline`; Day `edgeStructure`; Veld a 2px #1B2632 border with the name at 18/700 and the knock-out widened to 16dp.
items.accessibility: The label is `header: true`; the rule is decorative and excluded. At 2.0× the name wraps and the rule drops below the text block rather than running through it; Afrikaans wraps the same way.
items.amber: None, ever. It replaced an amber section marker and a numbered eyebrow precisely so it could not become a repeated accent.
items.screenshot: A faint horizontal line across the screen with a few words of warm off-white type sitting on it near the left edge, the line stopping and restarting around the words.

items.name: Stat tile (console)
items.purpose: One measured quantity, its movement, and its distance from target — as an instrument cell, not a card.
items.anatomy: REVISED throughout. No card, no border, no shadow, no radius AND no dividing lines: cells in a 2×2 cluster are separated by ground — s4 = 16 column gutter, s5 = 20 row gutter — because every inter-cell space must exceed every intra-cell space (max s2 = 8) and because `hairline` is 2.14:1 in Night and 1.18:1 in Day and cannot carry structure. Content hangs off each cell's own left edge, min-height 88 (a minimum, not a height). Order: eyebrow 11/700 uppercase `ink2`, tracking REVISED to +4%, permitted two lines and truncating only as a last resort at two; s2; figure `figure.l` 32/600 tabular JetBrains Mono `ink1`; delta on the figure's baseline s2 right; s2; a state line and then a freshness suffix (see states); an optional 3px meter — track `lifted`, fill `chartNeutral` #8B8271 (3.01:1 on track), target a 2px `ink2` tick breaking the track's top edge by 2dp. Contrast is quoted against `ground` (`ink3` 7.19:1, `bad` 7.78:1, `good` 11.76:1) because that is what the tile paints on; the word `raised` is deleted from this component so nobody reintroduces the card to make an old number true.
items.states: Default. REVISED note handling — two slots, not one, with declared precedence: a STATE line (provisional / no data / error / reconciliation, in that order) and a FRESHNESS suffix (' · as of 14:06') that appends where a state line exists and stands alone where none does, so a tile that is provisional AND stale can no longer lose its staleness. No data (#398): eyebrow unchanged, em dash at `figure.l` in `ink3` (not `ink1` — it is not a value), no delta, no meter, state line 'no visits in this window'. Never 0, never an arrow next to nothing. Provisional (#390): dotted `edgeControl` rule under the figure box plus the word. Off-target REVISED: carried by the meter's tick position and the state line only — the eyebrow triangle is deleted, because a half-filled triangle at the top-left of a cell that already shows a delta triangle beside the figure was two severities in one 88dp cell. Loading, error (em dash plus 'could not load' plus an inline 44dp ghost Retry), stale.
items.behaviour: REVISED: no count-up. The figure is present at first paint; the cluster enters with the shell's 320ms reveal. This deletes the horizontal jitter of a delta beside a growing digit count and the heaviest frame sequence on cold start. REVISED: the figure/delta Wrap is unconditional and width-driven, not gated on text scale — at 1.0× on 360dp a tile is 160dp wide and `figure.l` plus a '−19 pts' delta already does not fit, so the delta drops to its own line whenever the measured width demands it. Figures over 5 glyphs step `figure.l` → `figure.m` → FittedBox scaleDown inside a min-height box. Tappable only when the figure decomposes; press per the press model.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: figure `ink1` #1B2632, delta `good` #14664A / `bad` #8C1B2C, meter track `well` #E2DBCC with `chartNeutral` #676052 (4.52:1) and an `ink1` tick, press inverts. Veld: no meter at all — the figure and the word carry it, and the target prints as a second figure line 'target 75'; figure 32/700, note 14/600.
items.accessibility: One Semantics node: eyebrow, figure, delta direction as a word ('down 19 points'), state, freshness. Direction is the triangle first, colour second, the word third. Cluster collapses 2×2 → 1×4 on a LayoutBuilder width threshold, never on a scale guess. Eyebrow strings are checked at 1.4× their English width before ship, because uppercase plus tracking is the most space-hungry setting in the system and the eyebrow is the tile's only label channel.
items.amber: None. REVISED: the amber target tick is deleted outright — a target is an annotation, i.e. a label, and the law says amber is never a label. It was also the clearest case of a component's colour depending on its neighbours' arithmetic.
items.screenshot: Four unboxed cells in a 2×2 grid with clear black gutters between them and no lines at all: a tiny uppercase label, a large mono number, a small coloured triangle and figure beside it or beneath it, one grey line of context, and on one cell a thin bar with a small pale notch breaking its top edge.

items.name: Delta mark
items.purpose: The shape that says which way a number moved, so colour never has to.
items.anatomy: An 8px solid triangle plus a value at 13/600, s1 apart, on the owning figure's baseline — or on its own line beneath when the measured width demands it. Up: apex top. Down: apex bottom. No change: an 8 × 2 flat bar, not a triangle. A true minus U+2212, never a bracket, always tabular mono. Colour `good` for on-target movement and `bad` for off-target, so a falling stockout count is `good` with a down triangle.
items.states: Up-good, up-bad, down-good, down-bad, flat, and absent. Absent is the important one: with no comparable prior window the mark does not render and nothing takes its place — the state line says 'no prior window'. Never '0%' when the truth is 'nothing to compare'.
items.behaviour: Enters once with its figure on the shell's reveal; static thereafter, including on later value changes.
items.modes: Night `good` #6FE0AE / `bad` #FF7D8C. Day #14664A / #8C1B2C. Veld #0F5039 / #7A0F22 at weight 700, triangle 10px because glare eats small silhouettes.
items.accessibility: Announced as words before the number: 'down 19 points, off target'. The triangle is the non-colour channel; a greyscale screenshot still reads direction. Never the only content in a cell.
items.amber: None. The law forbids amber on a severity-coded delta — this is the rule the first dashboard draft broke.
items.screenshot: A small solid triangle pointing down in soft crimson with the figure minus-nineteen beside it, on the same baseline as the big number to its left.

items.name: Severity and measurement mark set
items.purpose: The console's whole severity vocabulary — one hue at two commitment levels, plus a silhouette, plus a word — and the one mark that means "not measured".
items.anatomy: Five marks, 12px unless stated. CRITICAL: filled triangle `badSolid` #E23C55; its row takes a 3px solid `bad` left bar 40dp tall. WATCH: half-filled triangle `bad` #FF7D8C; same bar at 40% alpha. ON TARGET: filled circle `good`. HELD / QUEUED: 10px square `comparison` #E08E71 — deliberately not a severity. NOT MEASURED: a 12px square filled with 45° hard-stop LinearGradient stripes. REVISED contrast and period: stripes are `ink3` #A79E8C on `lifted` (4.30:1) or on `ground` (7.19:1) at a 4dp period / 2px stroke — the old `inkMute` on `lifted` was 1.77:1 and at a 2dp period landed on sub-pixel boundaries on a 1x panel and averaged to the flat grey bar the hatch exists to not be. REVISED scope: this single hatch mark now covers BOTH "can't confirm" (#375) and "unscored", with the accompanying word carrying the case — hatch means "no measurement", and the absence of a mark now means exactly one thing: fine.
items.states: The five above, plus acknowledged/resolved (the mark stays, the row's ink drops to `ink2`, ' · acknowledged' appends — a resolved critical is still a critical that happened). There is no longer an "unknown, no mark" state; unknown is the hatch.
items.behaviour: Static. Never pulses — the pulse is reserved for the live amber on the day trail and a breathing severity would collide with it.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: `bad` #8C1B2C, `badSolid` #7A0F22 with white ink, `good` #14664A, `comparison` #A35139, hatch `ink3` #676052 on `well` #E2DBCC (4.52:1). Veld: marks 16px, critical a solid #7A0F22 block with white ink, hatch at a 3dp period / 2px stroke in #1B2632.
items.accessibility: Severity is announced FIRST in every row, before the title. Five distinct silhouettes survive greyscale, deuteranopia, print and a sun-washed panel. REVISED: the hatch never ships without its word — the decomposition sheet always had one; the ranked bar's no-value row and the trend chart's gap band now do too.
items.amber: None, ever. This component is why the 25–45° band stays free for the brand.
items.screenshot: A legend of five shapes: a solid crimson triangle, a half-filled one, a green circle, a warm brown square, and a pale square filled with coarse diagonal stripes you can count.

items.name: Decision row
items.purpose: One outlet that needs a manager to do something, with the reason and the number that proves it.
items.anatomy: REVISED separation. Soft full-width surface, no border, no radius, min-height 76 (14 pad, ~48 content, 14 pad) and a 12dp gap of ground to the next row, so the inter-row space is three times any intra-row leading and the gestalt does the work a 1.18:1 line could not. In Night a 1px `hairline` seam may sit in the middle of that gap as decoration; in Day it is not drawn at all. I decline the critique's alternative of a 1px `edgeControl` divider: at 6.02:1 it would out-shout the section rule, invert the page's hierarchy and rebuild the table look the console exists to avoid. Left: 3px severity bar at x = gutter, 40dp tall, vertically centred; content starts at 35dp whether or not a bar is present, so the column aligns. Title: outlet name, `title.m` 16/600 `ink1`, MIDDLE-truncated. s1. Reason: `body` 14/400 `ink2`, up to 2 lines. Right cluster: sparkline 64 × 20, s3, figure `figure.m` 22/600 tabular mono `ink1`.
items.states: Critical / watch / fine (no bar, no mark) / UNSCORED REVISED (the hatch square at the bar's position plus the word 'unscored' in the reason — a bar-less row now means 'fine' and nothing else). Pressed per the press model, including the leading `ink2` tick. Loading. No sparkline: the cell is omitted and the figure shifts right — never a fabricated shape. No figure: em dash `ink3`. Flagged: chips on their own line. Acknowledged. Stale. Locked by another manager: a `comparison` square and 'Being reviewed by Thabo M.', still tappable, read-only.
items.behaviour: Whole row is the hit target. Tap pushes the outlet detail, preserving scroll offset and filter on return. Long-press does nothing — a consequential list does not hide actions. Sparkline in a RepaintBoundary, cached to a Picture invalidated only on data change; no blur, shadow or gradient inside the list.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: the gap carries the separation alone, press inverts to the `lifted` ink block with `ground` ink. Veld: rows grow to ~96, 2px #1B2632 rules return because at 2px on white they are structural, the bar becomes a 6px solid block, and the sparkline is DROPPED (under 9:1 by construction) and replaced by the delta printed as a figure.
items.accessibility: One node: severity word, outlet name, reason, figure, 'opens outlet'. At 2.0× the sparkline drops first, then the figure moves onto its own line; the row grows, nothing clips. Middle truncation applies to the outlet name only.
items.amber: None. A sparkline's last dot is its row's severity colour — five amber dots on five rows was the exact repeated fill the law bans.
items.screenshot: Full-width bands of near-black separated by clear black gaps, each with a short crimson bar at its left edge, an outlet name in off-white, a grey sentence explaining what went wrong, a tiny grey zigzag with a single crimson dot at its end, and a large mono number.

items.name: Sparkline cell
items.purpose: Shape of the last few periods, next to the row it belongs to — context, not a chart.
items.anatomy: 64 × 20dp. Stroke 1.5px `chartNeutral` #8B8271, no fill, axis, gridline or label. Y-range is the series' own min/max with 2dp padding, so the shape is honest about movement while the row's figure carries the absolute value. Last point: a 3px filled dot in the ROW's severity colour. First point: nothing.
items.states: Default. Fewer than 2 points: the cell is omitted — never a flat line, which reads as 'stable' when the truth is 'unknown'. No endpoint for this metric: omitted permanently, and no surrounding copy implies one exists. Loading: a `well` block. All-equal values: a straight line renders, because the data genuinely is flat — distinguished from the omitted case by the dot being present.
items.behaviour: Static, non-interactive, never animated. RepaintBoundary plus a cached Picture invalidated only on data change; redrawn on skin change.
items.modes: Night `chartNeutral` #8B8271. Day #676052. Veld: not rendered — no token under 9:1 may draw a line, and a 1.5px stroke in sun is nothing; the row prints the delta as a figure instead.
items.accessibility: `ExcludeSemantics` — the row already announces direction and value in words. Never the only carrier of anything.
items.amber: None.
items.screenshot: A tiny grey zigzag about a thumbnail wide, ending in one small coloured dot, with no axes or labels.

items.name: Ranked bar row
items.purpose: Worst-first comparison across outlets, agents or territories, with one bar the answer is actually about.
items.anatomy: Row height 44. Label left, `body` 14/400 `ink1`, middle-truncated, max 40% of width. Track 6px, radius 3, `lifted` #2C3B4D, filling the remaining width minus a 56dp value column. Fill `chartNeutral` #8B8271 (3.01:1 on track). Value right, `figure.s` tabular mono. Rows s2 apart, worst first, always. FOCUS BAR (only when the screen's ledger nominates it) carries four channels: `flame600` fill, a 12dp amber gradient bloom beneath (flame900@0.55 → flame600@0.30 → transparent — a gradient, never a blur), a filled triangle at the bar's origin, and its label at `body.strong`. Negatives diverge left from a 1px centre axis with a `bad` HATCHED fill at the revised 4dp period.
items.states: Default, focus, negative, zero (a 2dp `edgeControl` cap at the origin so a zero bar is visibly zero and not a missing bar), NO-VALUE REVISED (track drawn, no fill, hatch mark at the label's left, value em dash `ink3`, and the words ' · not measured' are now mandatory rather than optional — hatch never ships alone), loading, too-many (cap at 8 plus a 44dp 'and 31 more' row), too-long label (middle truncation; the value column is never sacrificed).
items.behaviour: REVISED: bars draw in left-to-right over 320ms easeOutQuart, once per cluster, one controller, on first data build only. I hold against deleting this with the count-up: a bar's length IS the datum, where a spinning digit is a decoration, and 320ms on one controller costs less than the plate's image decode. Disabled under reduced motion, battery saver and Veld. Tap opens the entity. The focus bar never pulses.
items.modes: Night as above when nominated. Day AND Veld: focus is `ink1` fill (11.12:1 on the track) plus marker plus weight — never amber, because the single light block is spent on the commit. Veld: track 12px, 2px border, solid fills, no bloom, no radius.
items.accessibility: Each row: label, value, and 'highlighted' on the focus row. Focus is fill, bloom, marker and weight, because hue alone is 2.12:1 against the neutrals and 2.11:1 in greyscale. At 2.0× the label moves above its own track; below a 120dp track the component falls back to a plain label/value list.
items.amber: Zero by default (`lit: false`). Exactly one when a screen nominates it — the fill and its bloom counted as one emitted object. A chart with no headline claim has no amber bar.
items.screenshot: A stack of horizontal grey bars on darker tracks, worst at the top, with one bar glowing warm amber, a small amber triangle at its left end, its label bolder, and a soft warm haze bleeding below it.

items.name: Trend chart (console) + mandatory legend
items.purpose: Our series against a comparison and a target, over time, on a manager's phone.
items.anatomy: Height 208 phone, 260 at ≥600dp. Plot inset: left 40, right s4, top s3, bottom 28. Horizontal gridlines only, 1px `lifted`, 4 steps. Axis labels 12/400 tabular mono `ink3`. Our series: 2px line with a 12%→0 area fill (capped at 12%, because 18% behind the dashed terracotta is the tightest pair in the system) — `flame600` only when nominated, `ink1` otherwise, which in practice is every console screen that hosts it. Comparison: 1.5px `comparison` #E08E71 DASHED 4-3. Target: a 1px `edgeControl` dashed rule with its value at the right end. LEGEND is mandatory on every render: a 24dp row showing each series' 16 × 2 swatch drawn WITH its stroke pattern plus the name at `label` 13/500 `ink2`.
items.states: Default, single-series (legend still renders), no comparison (its legend row is absent rather than empty), fewer than 2 points (the chart is replaced by a left-aligned line: 'Two periods are needed to draw a trend. There is one.'), loading, error, PARTIAL SERIES REVISED (a genuine gap is drawn as a gap with a hatch band at the new `ink3` 4dp/2px setting AND a legend note 'no visits weeks 34–35' — the words are now mandatory), all-zero (drawn at zero with 'no stockouts recorded', because zero is a real value).
items.behaviour: Line draws in over 320ms once, one controller, off under reduced motion, battery saver and Veld. No tooltips on touch — a 360dp phone cannot hit a data point; a 44dp scrubber row beneath the legend steps period by period and writes values into a `raised` readout in tabular mono.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: our series `ink1` 2px solid with a 12% `ink1` area fill, comparison #A35139 dashed — amber leaves light grounds entirely. Veld: the chart is not drawn; a four-row figure list replaces it (this period, last period, median, target).
items.accessibility: One Semantics node summarising direction, start, end and the comparison in a sentence, plus the scrubber as the accessible data path. The dashed/solid distinction is load-bearing: amber and terracotta are 1.41:1 under deuteranopia. The legend renders every time.
items.amber: Zero by default. One when nominated — line plus area fill counted as a single object.
items.screenshot: A small dark chart with four faint gridlines, one off-white curve with a soft wash below it, a dashed terracotta curve crossing it, a dotted target line, and a short legend showing which pattern is which.

items.name: Flag chip (#393)
items.purpose: Names a condition that changes how a record should be read — without making it a severity badge.
items.anatomy: Outlined, transparent, 1px edge, radius 6, height 28 when non-interactive and 44 when tappable (the 28dp box centred in a 44dp hit area). Padding s2. A 14px glyph, s1, then `label` 13/500. Three variants: OUT OF FENCE — `bad` edge and ink, half-filled triangle, the measured distance appended in `mono.ident` ('Out of fence · 140 m'); FLAGGED FOR REVIEW — `bad` edge and ink, filled triangle; UNFINISHED VISIT — `edgeControl` edge, `ink2` ink, 10px square, on `well`; deliberately not a severity. Chips wrap in a Wrap with s2 spacing and run-spacing.
items.states: Each variant default, pressed (only when tappable, per the press model), collapsed (beyond three chips, the first two plus a '+2' that opens the record), resolved (the chip persists at `ink3` with ' · cleared' appended, because a cleared flag is history a reviewer needs).
items.behaviour: Tappable chips open the evidence for that flag — the geofence map, the review case, the unfinished visit. Non-tappable chips carry no press feedback at all, so they cannot be mistaken for controls.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: `bad` #8C1B2C, `edgeControl` #6E6657 on `well` #E2DBCC — `edgeStructure` is banned on the Day well at 2.99:1, so this chip takes `edgeControl` there. Veld: height 56, 2px #1B2632 borders on all three, ink #0E141A, and the filled-triangle variant sits on a solid #7A0F22 block with white ink.
items.accessibility: Each chip announces its full meaning, not its label: 'Watch: check-in was 140 metres outside the geofence.' Glyph silhouettes differ per variant; colour differs only between severity and non-severity. At 2.0× chips wrap and grow, never clip or scroll sideways.
items.amber: None. A flag is a label, and this is the component the law most obviously protects.
items.screenshot: Two or three small outlined tablets under a row of text: one crimson-edged with a half-filled triangle reading 'Out of fence · 140 m', one grey-edged with a small square reading 'Unfinished visit'.

items.name: Person row (#399)
items.purpose: Replaces every console screen that currently prints a raw database id where a person belongs.
items.anatomy: Min-height 56 (64 in field/Veld), growing freely. Left: a 40dp identity tile, radius 6, `raised` fill, holding a photo (BoxFit.cover, cacheWidth = dpr × 40) or two uppercase initials at `label` 13/500 `ink2`. s3. Then a column: REVISED — the name at `title.m` 16/600 `ink1` WRAPS TO TWO LINES and is never end-truncated; where a single line is structurally forced it middle-truncates as the outlet name does, and the full name is in the Semantics label regardless of what is painted. The critique is right: on a 200dp fraud row 'Nomsa Dlamini-Mkhize' and 'Nomsa Dlamini-Ndlovu' truncated to the same string, and the human being was getting less care than the store. Beneath at s1: role and context at `body` 14/400 `ink2`. A third line only when a machine identifier is genuinely needed, in `mono.ident` `ink3`. Trailing: an optional `figure.m` value or a 16px chevron.
items.states: Default. Unknown person: title 'Unknown agent' in `ink2`, second line 'Reference' plus the first 8 characters in `mono.ident`, a 44dp copy icon-button trailing — a raw UUID is never the title. Deactivated: ink to `ink2`, a 10px `comparison` square and the word. Loading. No photo: initials, always — never a generic silhouette. Self: ' · you' appends. Long name: wraps; the identity tile and trailing value never shrink.
items.behaviour: Whole row is the hit target when it navigates; press per the press model. The copy button fires a receipt toast ('Reference copied').
items.modes: Night as above. Day: tile `raised` #F4F0E8, press inverts. Veld: tile 56dp with a 2px border and no radius, initials 16/700, name 18/700 over up to three lines, second line 14/600.
items.accessibility: One node: full name, role, context, value. Initials are excluded (the name is right there). At 2.0× the trailing value moves beneath the second line and the row grows past 96dp. Afrikaans role labels wrap.
items.amber: None.
items.screenshot: A list row with a small rounded square holding two letters, a person's full name in off-white beside it wrapping onto a second line, a grey line reading 'Field agent · Kasi Corner Spaza', and a number or arrow at the far right.

items.name: Filter rail (territory + window)
items.purpose: The two questions every console figure depends on — which territory, over what window — always visible, never buried.
items.anatomy: A horizontally scrolling rail of outlined chips, height 44, radius 6, 1px `edgeControl` #7C93AC, transparent, `label` 13/500 `ink2`, s2 apart, from the gutter to the screen edge with a 20dp right bleed so it visibly continues. Window chips (7 days / 30 days / Quarter / All time), an 8dp gap with a 20dp vertical `hairline`, then the territory chip with a 12px chevron. SELECTED REVISED: `lifted` fill, `ink1` ink, label weight 700, edge stays `edgeControl` — never amber, on any screen. The earlier rule lit the selected chip on Alerts and not on The Floor purely because a slot was free, which made amber encode 'selected' (a label) and made a control's own vocabulary route-dependent. Sits s5 below the plate and s6 above the next block.
items.states: Default, selected, pressed, disabled (`inkMute` ink and a `meta` line beneath the rail: 'All time has no comparison window'). Territory chip open: a sheet of territories with outlet and agent counts. Filtered-to-empty: the rail stays and the content becomes the console empty state naming the filter. Loading territories: 'All territories', disabled.
items.behaviour: Tap toggles in 120ms with the press model's feedback. A change invalidates every provider on the screen together — panels that refresh at different moments quietly disagree, and a dashboard that contradicts itself is worse than one uniformly a minute old. Not reset by pull-to-refresh. Persists per session.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: selected is the `lifted` ink block with `ground` ink (9.43:1) — the press and the selection therefore share a vocabulary, which is correct: both mean 'this one'. Veld: chips 56 tall, 2px borders, selected a solid #1B2632 block with white ink, and the rail WRAPS to two rows rather than scrolling, because a horizontal scroll is a gesture a thumb in the sun loses.
items.accessibility: `Semantics(container:)` labelled 'Filters'; each chip a button with `selected:`. Selection is fill plus weight plus the semantics flag. At 2.0× chips grow and the rail wraps. Horizontal scroll never traps the page scroll.
items.amber: None, on any screen, ever. A filter chip has never been the most important lit thing in this product.
items.screenshot: A row of small outlined tablets under the hero image: '30 days' filled a shade lighter with bolder off-white type, then '7 days', 'Quarter', a faint divider, and 'Gauteng North' with a chevron.

items.name: Verdict control (fraud review)
items.purpose: Recording what a manager decided about a possibly-faked visit — the most consequential control in the product.
items.anatomy: Deliberately NOT a segmented control: three stacked full-width rows, because a segmented control invites a mis-tap on an irreversible judgement. Each row 56dp, radius 10, 1px `edgeControl`, transparent, padding s3; a 20px glyph, s3, then the verdict at `body.strong` 14/600 `ink1` with its consequence beneath at `meta` 12/400 `ink3`. Rows s2 apart. 'Not fraud — clear it' ('The visit keeps its score. The flag is recorded as cleared.'); 'Coach the agent' ('Opens a task assigned to you, due in 3 days.'); 'Escalate to investigation' ('Locks the visit and notifies the account owner.'). SELECTED: `lifted` fill, a filled 8px square at the far left, weight 700 — three cues, none of them colour. Escalate expands a required reason picker: 44dp outlined chips and, on Other, a 3-line trough. Below, s6: the commit, full width, 44dp, radius 10, `lifted` fill, 1px `flame600` rim, `ink1`, a 2px amber gradient bleed along the top edge, 'Record verdict'.
items.states: Nothing selected (commit disabled: `well`, `inkMute`, NO rim — a disabled button must not carry the screen's amber — with 'Choose a verdict' beneath). Selected. Escalate-without-reason ('Escalate needs a reason'). Committing (three travelling `ink2` dots, never a spinner; the rows lock). Committed (replaced in place by a `raised` block: the verdict as a sentence, the manager's name, the timestamp, and a 44dp 'Change this verdict' for 24 hours, then a `meta` lock line). Failed (returns to Selected unchanged plus a failure receipt with Retry — the verdict is never silently lost). Offline (commit stays enabled, records locally, 'Held — will send when there is signal'). Decided by someone else while open (the committed block plus a `bad`-edged note naming who and when, with the manager's choice preserved in a 'you had chosen Coach' line rather than discarded).
items.behaviour: Selection is 120ms with the press model, no scroll jump. The commit enters its busy state on touch-up, before the call. Escalate routes through the confirm sheet; clearing and coaching do not, because they are cheap and reversible and a second confirm on routine work trains people to tap through confirms. No swipe gesture anywhere.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: the commit is a solid `flame600` block with `onAmber` #1B2632 (8.55:1). Veld: rows 72dp with 2px borders, selected a solid #1B2632 block with white ink, commit a 64dp solid `flame600` block with `veld-ink` (10.34:1) that inverts to the ink block on press rather than lightening.
items.accessibility: A radio group: 'Verdict, 3 options'; each row announces verdict, consequence, then selected state. The commit announces its disabled REASON, not just 'disabled'. Targets 56. At 2.0× consequences wrap to three lines and rows pass 96dp; nothing is pinned.
items.amber: One when the screen nominates it — the rim plus its 2dp bleed as a single object. On the fraud case that nomination is spent here, so the evidence chart on the same screen is `ink1`.
items.screenshot: Three tall outlined rows each with an icon, a bold verdict and a smaller grey consequence; the middle one filled lighter with a small solid square at its left edge; below, a wide dark button with a thin warm amber outline and a faint glow along its top edge.

items.name: Confirm sheet
items.purpose: The one step back before an irreversible console action.
items.anatomy: Bottom sheet, radius 14 top, `surface`, 1px `edgeStructure`, grabber, scrim @72%, no blur, padding s5. In order: the action as a sentence at `title.l` 20/600, max 2 lines; s3; what will happen as up to three `body` `ink2` lines each with a 6px `ink3` square bullet; s3; the affected record in `mono.ident` `ink3` on a `well` block at radius 6; s6; two full-width stacked controls — the destructive commit (44dp, radius 10, `badSolid` #E23C55, `onBadSolid` ink, filled triangle glyph) then s2 then a ghost Cancel.
items.states: Default, committing (busy dots on the commit, Cancel disabled), failed (the sheet stays open with a `bad`-edged inline row above the buttons and a Retry), offline (the commit reads 'Hold and send later' and one line explains), dismissed (no side effect; the caller's selection survives).
items.behaviour: Opens 320ms. The destructive action is the TOP button — a thumb reaching the bottom-most control by habit should land on Cancel. Back and scrim both cancel. Never auto-dismisses on a timer.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: `surface` #FAF7F2, sh1, commit `badSolid` #7A0F22 with white ink (10.94:1). Veld: white, radius 0, 2px border, buttons 64dp.
items.accessibility: `scopesRoute`, announced as a dialog; focus lands on the headline, then the consequences, then Cancel — never on the destructive button. Its semantics include the consequence, not just the verb. At 2.0× the sheet scrolls internally and the two buttons stay pinned to the sheet's own commit zone, the one place pinning is correct.
items.amber: None. A destructive confirm is severity, and severity never touches amber.
items.screenshot: A dark panel over a dimmed screen: a question in large off-white type, three short grey bullet lines, a monospaced record code on a darker block, then a crimson button and a plain outlined Cancel.

items.name: Progress-to-reward bar (#396)
items.purpose: How close a contest, incentive or coverage target is to paying out — without turning progress into a light source.
items.anatomy: Full content width. Above the track: left, 'R 1 240 / R 1 500' at `figure.s` tabular mono `ink1`; right, 'Reward at R 1 500' at `meta` `ink3`. s2. Track 6px, radius 3, `lifted`. Fill `chartNeutral` #8B8271 (3.01:1 on track) — not amber, because a page of contests would repeat an amber fill. Threshold tick: 2px breaking the track's top edge by 2dp, `ink2` by default and `flame600` only where a single-contest detail nominates it in the ledger. s2. Beneath: `meta` `ink3`, 'Ends Friday 26 Sep · 4 days left'.
items.states: Not started (fill 0 plus a 2dp `edgeControl` cap at the origin so the track does not read as broken; '0 / R 1 500 — not started'). In progress. Reached (`good` fill, a filled 8px circle at the right end, 'Reached 24 Sep'). Exceeded (`good` to the tick, then a `good` hatch at the 4dp period beyond it, with the overage printed). Expired unreached (`chartNeutral` at 50%, a 10px `comparison` square, 'Closed 20 Sep — not reached'). No data (empty track, em dash, 'no qualifying visits yet'). Loading. Unknown threshold (no tick at all and 'threshold not set' — never a tick at a guessed position).
items.behaviour: Fill animates in over 320ms on first data build only, alongside the other bars on one controller. No pulse. Tappable rows open the contest; the press fills the ROW, not the bar.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: track `well` #E2DBCC, fill #676052 (4.52:1), tick `ink1`. Veld: a 16dp white rectangle with a 2px border, solid #1B2632 fill, the threshold a full-height 2px rule, and the percentage printed as a figure — in sun a bar's length is the only readable thing and a number removes the guess.
items.accessibility: One node with `value`: 'Progress to reward, 1 240 of 1 500 rand, 83 percent, 4 days left.' Reached is a word. At 2.0× the two labels stack; the track never shrinks. Hit box ≥ 44 when the row navigates.
items.amber: Zero by default, including in every list. Exactly one where a single-contest detail nominates the tick.
items.screenshot: A slim grey bar mostly filled with a warmer grey, a small pale notch breaking its top edge near the right end, a mono figure above left, 'Reward at R 1 500' above right, and a deadline line beneath.

items.name: Provisional / final figure and reconciliation line (#390)
items.purpose: Says out loud when a number is not yet the number, and what changed when it settled.
items.anatomy: Wraps any figure role and writes into the owner's STATE line, leaving the freshness suffix free. PROVISIONAL: the figure renders in `ink1` with a 1px `edgeControl` dotted rule (2dp dash, 2dp gap) the figure's width, 2dp below its box; the state line reads 'Provisional' at `label` 13/500 `ink2` preceded by a 10px `comparison` square. FINAL AND CHANGED: the figure shows the final value at full weight, no dotted rule, and the state line reads — REVISED pronoun — 'Scored 71 — the phone showed 84 when the visit closed.' The manager never saw 84; the second-person string belongs to the agent app and is a different string, not a shared one. Both numbers sit in that sentence at 12px mono, so there are never two competing large figures. FINAL AND UNCHANGED: nothing renders — confirming the expected is noise.
items.states: Provisional, final-changed, final-unchanged, final-unknown ('The final score has not arrived. This is what the phone computed.'), superseded ('Scored 71 — the phone showed 84, then 79 after the recount'), disputed (a half-filled triangle and 'Under review since 14:20' in `bad`).
items.behaviour: When a provisional value becomes final in a live session the figure cross-fades over 200ms — it does not animate its digits, because that reads as a second measurement. The state line enters with a 4dp rise. Tapping it opens the visit that produced both numbers.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: dotted rule `edgeControl` #6E6657, `comparison` #A35139. Veld: the dotted rule becomes a 2px solid #1B2632 underline (dots disappear in glare) and 'Provisional' sets at 16/700.
items.accessibility: 'On-shelf availability, 71 percent, final. Earlier shown as 84 percent.' The dotted rule is never the only cue — the word is always present. At 2.0× the sentence wraps to three lines and the tile grows.
items.amber: None. Uncertainty is carried by `comparison`, hatch and words — never by the torch.
items.screenshot: A large mono number with a fine dotted line beneath it and the word 'Provisional' below that; settled, the number is clean with one grey sentence reading 'Scored 71 — the phone showed 84 when the visit closed.'

items.name: Held-work row (console mirror of the outbox, #391)
items.purpose: Shows a manager what is sitting unsent on an agent's phone, so a quiet scorecard is never mistaken for a lazy agent.
items.anatomy: Min-height 56, `well` #141D27 fill, radius 0, full-bleed to the gutters, 1px `hairline` above and below — legal here because the fill step plus the mark plus the words already separate it, and the rule is decoration. Left at the gutter: a 10px `comparison` #E08E71 square (6.70:1 on well). s3. `body` 14/400 `ink1`: '4 visits held on this phone'; beneath at s1, `meta` `ink3`: 'oldest 2 h 14 m · last sent 11:48'. Trailing: a 16px chevron.
items.states: HELD (the normal state of South African field connectivity, and never red). SENDING (three travelling `ink2` dots replace the square; 'Sending 4 visits…'). RETRYING ('Retrying at 14:20', time in `mono.ident`). STUCK, over 24 h or three failed retries (a 1px `bad` edge top and bottom, the square becomes a half-filled triangle, 'Stuck — 4 visits held since yesterday 09:12', plus a 44dp ghost 'Message the agent'). NONE HELD (the row does not render — absence of held work needs no announcement). UNKNOWN ('Held work unknown — this agent's app is on an older version', `inkMute`, non-tappable).
items.behaviour: Tap expands in place over 200ms to list each held visit — outlet, age in `mono.ident`, size in kB. Never offers a 'force send': the manager does not hold the data and a button that cannot work is worse than none.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: `well` #E2DBCC, `comparison` #A35139, and because `edgeStructure` is banned on the Day well the stuck state takes a 1px `bad` #8C1B2C edge. Veld: 2px border, 16px square, text 17/600, sub-rows 64dp.
items.accessibility: 'Held work: 4 visits held on this phone, oldest 2 hours 14 minutes. Expandable.' Stuck announces 'Watch' first. Square, dots and triangle are three silhouettes. Hit box 56.
items.amber: None. An amber queue chip would make load-shedding look like a fault — the single most important non-amber decision in the system.
items.screenshot: A slightly lighter dark band with a small warm-brown square at its left, '4 visits held on this phone' in off-white, a smaller grey line of times beneath, and a chevron at the right.

items.name: Console skeleton set
items.purpose: Says the console is loading in the exact shape of what is coming — without shimmer, and without pretending to be live.
items.anatomy: Static `well` blocks in the precise geometry of the real content: plate → a full-bleed block at the computed plate height with no strip light; stat cell → an 11px block 40% wide, a 32px block 60% wide, a 12px block 70% wide at the real s2 gaps, in the real 16/20 cluster gutters; decision row → a 16px block 55% wide and a 14px block 85% wide with a 64 × 20 block right, at the real 76dp min-height and 12dp gap; ranked bar → the real track in `well`. After 600ms a single 2px `ink2` rule travels the top edge of the loading region at 1400ms linear.
items.states: Under 600ms: blocks only, no travelling rule (a rule that flashes on a fast response is worse than none). Over 600ms: blocks plus rule. Over 8s: the rule continues and a `meta` line appears, 'Still loading. The connection is slow.', with a 44dp ghost Cancel. Over 20s: the region becomes the inline error. Partial: resolved panels render, unresolved keep their own skeleton, and `skipLoadingOnReload` keeps the last data on screen while a filter change refetches.
items.behaviour: One shared application Ticker drives the travelling rule, the busy dots and the day trail's pulse — three subscribers, one ticker. Disabled under `MediaQuery.disableAnimations`, battery saver and Veld.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: blocks `well` #E2DBCC, rule `ink2` #4A4437. Veld: NO skeleton — the word 'Loading' at 17/600 on the left gutter and nothing else, because a grey block in sun is indistinguishable from a broken screen.
items.accessibility: The region is `liveRegion` labelled 'Loading …' announced once, not per block; blocks are excluded. The travelling rule is `ink2`, never amber — a skeleton is loading, not live, and the first draft's pulsing amber told a manager a placeholder was real-time data.
items.amber: None, by rule, and this is the one place the law was accidentally broken before.
items.screenshot: The dashboard's exact layout in flat dark-grey blocks — a big band, four cells in a clean grid, five row shapes — with one faint pale line sliding across the top edge.

items.name: Inline error and retry
items.purpose: Says which part failed, in place, without taking the rest of the screen down with it.
items.anatomy: Replaces only the failing region at that region's own height (min 44). Left at the gutter: a 12px half-filled triangle in `bad`. s3. A column: what failed at `body` 14/400 `ink1` ('Could not load the territory scores.'); beneath at s1 the reason in plain words at `meta` `ink3` ('The server did not answer.' / 'No connection.' / 'You do not have access to this territory.'). Trailing or beneath, whichever fits: a ghost Retry, 44dp, radius 10, 1px `edgeControl`, `ink1`. No panel, no card, no red fill.
items.states: Network, server, permission (NO Retry — retrying a 403 is a lie; a ghost 'Ask for access' opens the account owner as a person row), not-found (the region collapses to one `meta` line and the filter resets), rate-limited (Retry disabled with a live countdown in `mono.ident`), retrying (busy dots), repeated failure (after the third attempt the reason adds 'Three attempts have failed' and a ghost 'Copy diagnostics' copies route, time and error code in `mono.ident`).
items.behaviour: An error NEVER renders as a spinner — a spinner reads as 'still loading' and never recovers, which is the exact bug this replaced. Keep that sentence in the codebase. Retry invalidates only that region's provider; the region keeps its scroll position so nothing jumps beneath it.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: `bad` #8C1B2C, press inverts. Veld: triangle 16px, message 17/600, Retry 64dp with a 2px border.
items.accessibility: `liveRegion`, announced 'Error: could not load the territory scores. The server did not answer. Retry button.' Severity word first; the triangle is the non-colour channel. Hit box 44.
items.amber: None.
items.screenshot: A small crimson half-filled triangle beside two lines explaining what failed and why, with a plain outlined Retry, sitting in the gap where a chart should have been.

items.name: Empty state (console)
items.purpose: A settled answer of 'nothing here', distinguished from loading and from failure.
items.anatomy: REVISED and much plainer. Left-aligned, never centred. No illustration: the 64px line drawing is cut, because it encoded nothing, needed a bespoke asset on each of twelve screens, and was the one thing in the console that could have belonged to any other app. Headline REVISED to `title.l` 20/600 `ink1` at every text scale — the old `display` 40 was the system's largest non-hero type spent on the least important state, and the fact that it already dropped to `title.l` at 2.0× was an admission. Optional 12px mark before the headline where one is truthful. s3, one `body` 14/400 `ink2` line that names the next real action rather than the absence — the part that was always doing the work. s5, one ghost button, 44dp. Padding s8 top and bottom.
items.states: Genuinely empty ('No alerts have fired. Rules evaluate on every visit submit.'), empty because of a filter ('No agents are assigned to Gauteng North.' plus 'Clear the territory filter' — naming the filter turns a dead end into an action), empty because nothing is set up (hands off to the first-run board), empty after a clear-out ('Everything triaged.' with a filled `good` circle — a real achievement may read as one), resolved-only ('Nothing open. 12 acknowledged this week.' plus 'Show acknowledged').
items.behaviour: Static; the button is the only interactive element. Enters with its section on the shell's 200ms reveal.
items.modes: Night as above. Day standard, press inverts. Veld: headline 20/700, body 17/600, button 64dp with a 2px border.
items.accessibility: Headline is `header: true`. At 2.0× nothing changes size, because it is already at a size that survives — the block simply grows as text wraps. Afrikaans headlines wrap to three lines with nothing to displace.
items.amber: None. Nothing is happening, so nothing is lit.
items.screenshot: A left-aligned block: one line of off-white type at heading size, a single grey line of guidance beneath it, and a plain outlined button — hanging off the same left line as the rest of the screen, with a lot of black around it.

items.name: Offline / stale banner
items.purpose: Tells a manager the figures are from a moment ago, without calling normal South African connectivity an error.
items.anatomy: The first child of the content column, full-bleed, radius 0, min-height 44, `well` fill, 1px `hairline` bottom. Left at the gutter: a 10px `comparison` square. s3. `body` 14/400 `ink2`: 'Showing data from 14:06 — no connection since.' Trailing: a 44dp ghost Retry. It PUSHES content down and never overlays, because a banner that covers the first row hides the worst outlet.
items.states: OFFLINE (as above, never red). SERVER ERROR (a 1px `bad` edge top and bottom, the square becomes a half-filled triangle: 'Some figures could not be refreshed at 14:06.'). RECONNECTING (busy dots). RECOVERED (a `good` outline with a filled circle and 'Up to date' for 3 seconds, then a 200ms exit — a recovery that lingers becomes furniture). PARTIALLY STALE (the banner does not render at all; each stale tile appends its own freshness suffix, because a global banner for a local staleness overstates the problem). AUTH EXPIRED (hands off to Session ended).
items.behaviour: REVISED insertion, which was displacing the list under a reaching thumb: the banner is committed after 3 seconds of confirmed failure but is INSERTED only when no pointer has been down for 500ms and either the scroll offset is 0 or the list is at rest, and then over a 200ms SizeTransition so the eye tracks it. It is never inserted under an active pointer or mid-fling; until it can insert, the header's sync affordance carries the state. Retry refetches everything. It never blocks interaction: stale data is still data.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: `well` #E2DBCC, `comparison` #A35139, `bad` #8C1B2C. Veld: 64dp, 2px borders top and bottom, 16px square, 17/600.
items.accessibility: `liveRegion` announced once on state change, not on every rebuild. Square, triangle, dots and circle are four silhouettes. Retry hit box 44.
items.amber: None. Held and offline are `comparison` warm neutral — a torch-coloured offline banner would make the brand mean 'broken'.
items.screenshot: A narrow slightly-lighter band at the top of the dashboard with a small warm-brown square, 'Showing data from 14:06 — no connection since', and a plain Retry at the right.

items.name: Console receipt toast
items.purpose: Confirms that a tap actually did something, and offers the way back.
items.anatomy: Min-height 44, max width 320 or viewport − 32, radius 10, `surface` fill, 1px `edgeStructure`, no shadow in Night. Padding s3: a 12px glyph, s2, `body` 14/400 `ink1`, then an optional ghost action at `label` 13/500 with a 44dp hit box. Anchored bottom-LEFT, 16dp from the gutter and 92dp above the safe area, so it never sits under the pill or the circle.
items.states: SUCCESS (filled `good` circle, 4s, optional Undo). FAILURE (half-filled `bad` triangle, 8s, Retry — failures get twice the dwell because they need reading). INFO (10px `ink3` square, 4s). HELD (10px `comparison` square: 'Held — will send when there is signal', 6s). STACKED (a second replaces the first immediately; a third within 2s collapses all into '3 alerts acknowledged' with one Undo that reverses all three). PERSISTENT (an unrecoverable failure stays until dismissed, with a 44dp close).
items.behaviour: Enters 200ms with an 8dp rise, exits 200ms. Undo reverses the optimistic change and re-expands the collapsed row. Swipe-down dismisses. Reduced motion: instant.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: `surface` #FAF7F2 plus sh2. Veld: white, radius 0, 2px border, 64dp, 17/600, dwell doubled to 8s because reading in sun is slower.
items.accessibility: `liveRegion` announced once. The action is a real focusable button, never gesture-only. Glyph silhouettes carry success, failure and held. Never the only confirmation of a destructive action — the record on screen changes too.
items.amber: None.
items.screenshot: A small dark rounded panel near the bottom-left with a thin outline, a tiny green circle, 'Alert acknowledged', and 'Undo' at its right.

items.name: Photographic plate (console) and its fallback
items.purpose: The hero band on The Floor: a real shelf from the territory the manager is about to act on, made cinematic by one strip of light.
items.anatomy: REVISED in four ways the critique forced. (1) HEIGHT: min(clamp(0.44 × vh, 200, 360), vh − 440); under 200 the plate does not render and the 96dp collapsed hero band replaces it — the old 0.44-of-the-fold left 22dp of list on a 360×640 A04. (2) SOURCE: the frame comes from the TERRITORY's qualifying pool, chosen once per day, NOT from the first decision row — a figure printed over a photograph of one named store is read as being about that store, and no eyebrow overrides a picture. (3) VISIBLE PROVENANCE: a `meta` `ink3` caption at the TOP of the text-safe zone names the outlet and capture time ('Kasi Corner Spaza · 17 Sep 06:40'), so the image is visibly a specimen and the hero cluster below is visibly about the territory. (4) BYTES: baked lossy WebP with alpha at q≈72 under a hard server-enforced 60 kB cap, not PNG — the old alpha-dissolve forced lossless and 400–900 kB per open on a prepaid bundle. Still baked server-side (12% chroma, no pixel above `plateCeiling` #474747, edge dissolve in the alpha), so the client draws one `Image` with cacheWidth and spends zero ShaderMask, saveLayer or ImageFiltered. STRIP LIGHT: a 2px `flame600` line at y = 0.38h clamped out of the lower 40%, with a 48dp gradient bloom above it — a gradient is the blur of a line, at zero cost. TEXT-SAFE ZONE: a bottom-up scrim (ground 0% → 80%) over the lower 52%, or 58% when the plate is under 240dp. HERO CLUSTER at the bottom-left: eyebrow ('GAUTENG NORTH · WEEK 38'), s2, the figure at `hero.figure` 72/600 (or `hero.figure.compact` 56 whenever the plate is under 260dp) with a 20px caret and the delta on its baseline in `bad`/`good`, s2, and REVISED the lead indicator's one line folded in here rather than repeated as a separate rail 84dp below.
items.states: Real plate. FALLBACK (no eligible frame — POPIA face detection, wrong territory, fraud-flagged, failed luma variance): five horizontal rules receding in perspective at 0.30 → 0.04 opacity in `flame600`, their SPACING driven by the territory's real OSA trend, so a shelf reads tighter when availability is worse. It is generated from data, never a placeholder. FIRST-RUN FALLBACK: the same rules in `edgeControl`, evenly spaced, amber withheld because there is nothing to light. DARK FRAME (mean luma < 18%) REVISED: a 2px `comparisonWash` edge and the caption 'Dark frame — mean brightness 11%'. The old 'Shot under load-shedding' asserted a cause from a measurement — the same pixels come from a cold room, a thumb over the lens, or a deliberately obscured shot — and on a fraud case it put the accused's excuse in the product's own voice. LOADING: a `well` block at the computed height. COLLAPSED: a preference shipping on day one reduces the plate to a 96dp hero band with no image.
items.behaviour: REVISED load order: the decision rows render first and the plate's image request starts after the list's first frame — the list must never wait on a photograph. Reveal 320ms, opacity plus a 1.02→1.00 scale on the image only, with the bloom fading in over the last 120ms so the light appears to switch on. No count-up on the hero figure. 'Territory health' opens the decomposition sheet; the image itself is not tappable.
items.modes: Night as described. Day: the baked image is kept but the strip light is REMOVED for a 2px `ink1` rule at the same y — amber on a light-ground photograph is decoration, not emitted light — and the scrim inverts to Palladian. Veld: no plate at all; the hero cluster renders on white at 72/700 with the delta at 17/700.
items.accessibility: A real `semanticLabel` naming outlet and capture time, or 'Generated shelf illustration'. The hero cluster is a separate node read before the image. Worst measured cases: `ink1` on the scrim over a full-value strip light 10.56:1, eyebrow 7.15:1, and the folded lead indicator's `bad` outline 5.21:1 on that same worst-case pixel. `hero.figure` caps at 1.6× text scale — the one documented exception, declared in the token — then falls to `hero.figure.compact` then to FittedBox scaleDown.
items.amber: One when nominated, and The Floor does nominate it: the strip light, line plus bloom counted as a single object. The data-driven fallback's rules count as one; the first-run fallback and every Day and Veld variant carry zero.
items.screenshot: A near-monochrome photograph of a shop shelf across the top of the phone, almost black, with one horizontal warm amber line glowing softly upward; a small grey caption naming the shop and the time sits at the top of the darkened lower band, and in the bottom-left corner a small uppercase territory label, an enormous off-white 72, a crimson triangle with −19, and one grey line reading 'OSA 61% · Coverage 78%'.

items.name: Lead indicator (inline and rail)
items.purpose: Breaks the three-equal-chips convention on purpose: on-shelf availability is what sends someone to an outlet, and coverage and price compliance are not its peers.
items.anatomy: REVISED into two presentations rather than one. INLINE (used on The Floor, inside the plate's hero cluster, directly beneath the hero figure): a single `meta`/`label` line — 'OSA 61%' at `figure.s` 16/600 `ink1` with a half-filled `bad` triangle when off target, then ' · Coverage 78% · Price compliance 91%' at `meta` `ink3`. No outline, no second block, no 84dp of repeated pattern below a figure that is already a figure. RAIL (used on every screen with no plate — Alerts, Tasks, Territories, Fraud): the dominant figure at `figure.l` 32/600 tabular mono with its label at `label` `ink2`, a severity triangle, and a 1px `bad` outline at radius 6 with s2 padding wrapping the cluster — outline, never fill — with the subordinates on one `meta` line beneath. The count of subordinates varies by territory; it is not fixed at three because a reference had three.
items.states: On target (no outline, no triangle). Watch (outline plus half-filled triangle). Critical (a solid `badSolid` block with `onBadSolid` ink and a filled triangle, subordinates still on the ground beneath). No data (em dash at `figure.l` in `ink3`, subordinates replaced by 'no visits in this window'). One subordinate or none (renders what exists, or omits the line — never padded to three). More than four (' · +3 more' opening the full indicator list). Loading.
items.behaviour: No count-up. Tappable: opens the metric's own trend; the press fills the cluster's bounds only and takes the leading tick.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: `bad` #8C1B2C outline, `badSolid` #7A0F22 with white ink. Veld: figure 32/700, outline a 2px #1B2632 border, critical a solid #7A0F22 block, and each subordinate gets its own 64dp row rather than a comma line — density halves outdoors.
items.accessibility: 'On-shelf availability, 61 percent, watch. Coverage 78 percent. Price compliance 91 percent.' Severity is announced with the figure. Outline plus triangle plus word carry the state. At 2.0× the subordinate line wraps and the triangle drops to its own line.
items.amber: None, in either presentation. This is a severity-coded figure and the law forbids amber on one.
items.screenshot: Inline: one line under the huge 72 reading 'OSA 61%' with a small crimson half-triangle, then smaller grey text listing coverage and price compliance. Rail: the same figure standing alone at 32px inside a thin crimson outline with the subordinates beneath.

items.name: Console icon button
items.purpose: The component that makes the audit's 26 unlabelled IconButtons impossible to recreate.
items.anatomy: 44 × 44 hit box (56 in Veld), no fill, no border by default, a 20px 2px-stroke glyph centred in `ink2`. `semanticLabel` is a REQUIRED non-nullable constructor argument — a build fails without it, so the omission cannot recur. Optional 1px `edgeControl` outline at radius 10 when it stands alone rather than in a header row.
items.states: Default, pressed (glyph to `ink1`, `lifted` fill at radius 10, scale 0.98, haptic), disabled (`inkMute` #4C6079, deliberately sub-AA because disabled controls are exempt under 1.4.3 and must look disabled; a `meta` line elsewhere names why — never a tooltip alone), busy (three travelling 4px `ink2` dots replace the glyph), toggled-on (`lifted` fill, `ink1` glyph, `Semantics(toggled: true)`), destructive (glyph `bad`, and it always routes through the confirm sheet).
items.behaviour: 120ms press. No long-press behaviours anywhere. Tooltips on desktop only and never as the sole label.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: glyph `ink2` #4A4437, press inverts to the `lifted` ink block with `ground` glyph. Veld: 56 × 56, 24px glyph at 3px stroke, 2px border always present because an unbordered glyph in sun has no edge.
items.accessibility: The required label is the whole point. Toggles use `Semantics(toggled:)`. Never smaller than 44 (56 in Veld) even at a 20px glyph. Focus ring 2px `flame700` #FFCB94 (10.38:1 on surface, 9.11:1 on raised) — transient, singular, and exempt from the ledger for the same reason the nav slot is.
items.amber: None at rest; the keyboard focus ring only, uncounted.
items.screenshot: A small two-stroke refresh glyph in warm grey with generous invisible space around it; pressed, a faint lighter rounded square appears behind it.

items.name: Pagination / more-below footer
items.purpose: Stops a first page from reading as the whole truth, which is what a cut list always does.
items.anatomy: Row height 44, `well` fill, full-bleed, 1px `hairline` above. At the gutter, `meta` 12/400 `ink3`: 'Showing the 20 riskiest of 74.' On a second line at s1: 'Narrow by territory to see the rest.' Trailing: a 44dp ghost 'Filter'. No 'Load more' button, because the API serves a first page and a button that cannot deliver is dishonest chrome.
items.states: More below. Exactly one page (absent). Unknown total ('Showing the first 20. There are more.' — never a fabricated total). Hard cap ('Showing the first 200 agents. Filter by territory to narrow.'). Filtered under the cap (absent). Unscored records (#236's honest case): a second `meta` line — '6 submitted visits have not been scored yet and are not listed here.' — because an unscored visit is not a clean one and a short list must never read as 'nothing suspicious'.
items.behaviour: Static except the ghost action, which scrolls to the filter rail and opens the territory sheet.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: `well` #E2DBCC, `ink3` #676052 (4.52:1 — the binding Day case). Veld: 64dp, 2px border, 14/600.
items.accessibility: Announced as part of the list's own semantics so a screen-reader user reaching the bottom learns the list was cut. Hit box 44.
items.amber: None.
items.screenshot: A slightly lighter strip at the bottom of a list with two small grey sentences on the left and a plain 'Filter' at the right.

items.name: The Floor (manager home)
items.purpose: Answers one question on a 360×640dp phone: what is broken, and who is fixing it.
items.anatomy: REVISED stack, arithmetic first. (1) PLATE, full-bleed at min(clamp(0.44 × vh, 200, 360), vh − 440), sourced from the territory's daily qualifying frame, captioned with its outlet and time, one strip light, and the hero cluster at the bottom-left carrying the eyebrow, the composite figure with its delta, the FOLDED lead indicator line, and 'Territory health' as a tappable. (2) s5, FILTER RAIL, selected chip `lifted` + weight, never amber. (3) s6, SECTION RULE 'Needs a decision 5' — the lead indicator rail and the 40dp of deliberate nothing are both gone from the phone layout; the 40dp survives only at ≥600dp. (4) DECISION ROWS at 76dp min with 12dp ground gaps, worst first. (5) 'and 11 more need a decision' as a 44dp `meta` row into the full worklist. (6) SECTION RULE 'Today's field' with three rows: agents on the map, held work, and today's coverage as a progress bar with an `ink2` tick. (7) Bottom pad 124dp. At 360×640 that is plate 200 + 132 of chrome + 208dp of visible list = two full rows and 32dp of the third; at 412×892, three rows and a half.
items.states: DEFAULT. LOADING (skeleton in exact geometry; the list resolves before the plate by design). PARTIAL. OFFLINE (banner inserts under the pointer-idle rule and pushes the plate down; every figure still rendered and tappable, each gaining its freshness suffix). ERROR PER REGION. PLATE FALLBACK. PLATE BELOW 200dp (the collapsed 96dp hero band, no image). FIRST RUN (hands off to the no-data board — The Floor is never a scoreboard of zeros). NOTHING NEEDS A DECISION (the rule stays; beneath it 'Everything triaged.' with a `good` circle and a ghost 'Show what was closed this week'). TOO MANY (5 plus the more-row, always). 2.0× TEXT (hero 72 → 56 → FittedBox, the delta wraps, sparklines drop from every row, the plate falls to its 200 floor, and the guarantee degrades to one full row — the declared minimum).
items.behaviour: Pull-to-refresh and an explicit Refresh button, both invalidating every provider together. Reveal 320ms with a 40ms stagger over plate, rail, rule and the first row; no count-up anywhere. Rows push the outlet and return to the same scroll offset and filter. Tapping the circle opens Raise a task / Assign a visit. Frame budget: 0 BackdropFilter, 0 ShaderMask, 0 ImageFiltered, 0 BoxShadow, 1 image decode deferred behind the list, ≤ 6 gradient decorations (plate scrim 1, bloom 1, ground falloff 2), 5 cached sparkline Pictures.
items.modes: Night × Console default. Day × Console: the plate keeps its image and loses the strip light for a 2px `ink1` rule, the nav active is the `lifted` block, and the screen's one amber block is the primary circle when there is an expected next move. Veld × Field: no plate, no sparklines, no charts; the hero figure on white, the lead indicator as its own 64dp block, three decision rows at ~96dp with 2px borders, a docked nav, and one amber commit block ('Raise a task').
items.accessibility: Reading order: plate caption, hero cluster with its folded indicator, filters, each section header, each row severity-first. Rows ≥ 76. Colour is never alone: severity is bar + triangle + word + position, the delta is triangle + word, held is square + word, unmeasured is hatch + word. Golden tests assert the visible row count at three widths and two text scales.
items.amber: TWO, counted: the nav pill's active block (exempt chrome) and the plate's strip light (the screen's one nomination). Because the ledger is now a screen-level nomination rather than a per-component default, no other object on this screen has to be talked out of being amber — the filter chip, the coverage tick and every sparkline dot are unlit by construction.
items.screenshot: A phone screen that is almost entirely black.
