The top third is a crushed photograph of a shop shelf with one warm amber line glowing across it, a small grey caption naming the shop and time, and in its lower-left corner a huge off-white 72 with a crimson −19 and one grey line of OSA and coverage. Below: a row of outlined filter tablets, a faint line with 'Needs a decision 5' on it, and two and a bit full-width bands of text each with a short crimson bar at the left, a grey sentence, a tiny sparkline and a mono number. A dark floating bar with one amber block hovers at the bottom.

items.name: First-run / no-data board
items.purpose: What a brand-new client sees instead of a scoreboard of zeros.
items.anatomy: (1) FIRST-RUN FALLBACK PLATE, 240dp, five evenly spaced receding rules in `edgeControl` — deliberately unlit — with a `meta` caption: 'No shelf yet. This becomes your territory's availability when the first visits land.' (2) s8, headline at `display` 40/600. I HOLD here against the critique's blanket demotion: this is the one screen in the console with nothing else on it, seen once per tenant, and the sentence 'Nothing has been measured yet.' is the entire content of the view — `display` is declared as this screen's exclusive use, and the empty-state component no longer competes for it. (3) s3, one `body` line: 'Four things have to exist before the console has anything to say.' (4) s6, the SETUP LADDER: four 64dp rows sharing the agent ladder's grammar — a 28dp radius-6 glyph tile with a 2px border joined vertically by a 2px rule, empty ring / half-filled / solid tick — 'Add outlets', 'Add agents', 'Draw a territory', 'First visit lands', each with a `meta` count. The first incomplete row carries a ghost action. (5) s7, the primary: full width, 44dp, `lifted` + 1px `flame600` rim + 2px bleed, 'Add your first outlets'. (6) s8, SECTION RULE 'What this board will show'. (7) The real stat cluster in its no-data state — eyebrows intact, em dashes in `ink3`, 'no visits in this window', no deltas, no zeros — the instrument, unlit. (8) s6, one `meta` line: 'These fill in as visits are submitted. Nothing here is a zero — it is an absence.'
items.states: NOTHING AT ALL. PARTLY SET UP (rungs fill, the headline becomes 'Two things left.', the primary moves to the next rung, and the cluster lights cell by cell — a half-lit instrument is the honest picture). OUTLETS BUT NO VISITS (plus a ghost 'Build a beat plan'). SETUP COMPLETE BUT WINDOW EMPTY (NOT first-run: the normal Floor renders with no-data tiles and a ghost 'Widen to 30 days' — the distinction between never-measured and not-measured-lately is the point of this screen). LOADING. ERROR per region; the ladder is local state and never fails. ROLE-LIMITED (ghost actions replaced by 'Ask your account owner to add outlets.' and the owner's person row). 2.0× (headline falls to `title.l`, rungs pass 96dp, tiles hold at 28dp).
items.behaviour: No animation on the ladder — nothing has happened yet, so nothing draws in. The plate does not reveal; it is simply there. Each action pushes its creation form and the board advances the rung on return with a single 200ms fill of the glyph tile: the one moment of motion on the screen, and it is earned.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: rules in `edgeControl` #6E6657, the primary a solid `flame600` block with `onAmber` (8.55:1). Veld: no plate, rungs 96dp with 2px borders, primary a 64dp solid amber block.
items.accessibility: The ladder is a list: 'Step 1 of 4, Add outlets, not started.' Rung state is ring / half / tick plus the word. No-data tiles announce 'no data, no visits in this window' — never '0'. Actions ≥ 44.
items.amber: TWO, counted: the nav pill (exempt chrome) and the primary button's rim (the nomination). Under the revised ledger the nav no longer has to go dark for this screen to be legal, which removes the one behaviour that would have looked like a bug.
items.screenshot: A dark screen topped by five receding grey shelf lines, then a large off-white 'Nothing has been measured yet.', a vertical ladder of four small square tiles joined by a line, a wide dark button with a warm amber outline, then a faint rule and four unboxed cells each showing a label, a long dash, and 'no visits in this window'.

items.name: Alerts worklist
items.purpose: Everything a rule fired on, in the order a manager should deal with it.
items.anatomy: (1) Header at the gutter: `title.l` 'Alerts' plus a 44dp Refresh, with 'Rules evaluate on every visit submit.' beneath and a ghost 'Manage rules' trailing. (2) s6, LEAD INDICATOR RAIL — not three equal cells, because critical and acknowledged are not peers: the open critical count at `figure.l` with a filled triangle and a `bad` outline, and beneath it '9 warnings · 23 acknowledged'. (3) s6, FILTER RAIL (Open · 7 / Acknowledged / All, then a severity chip), selected chip `lifted` plus weight — never amber. (4) s8, SECTION RULE with the visible count. (5) DECISION ROWS at 76dp with 12dp gaps: the alert message as the title, the reason beneath carrying the rule in `mono.ident` and the outlet ('OSA_BELOW_50 · Kasi Corner Spaza'), flag chips on their own line, and a 40dp evidence thumbnail at radius 10 where a photo exists — no placeholder where it does not. Ghost actions: 'View visit' (only when a visitId exists) and 'Acknowledge'. (6) Pagination footer.
items.states: DEFAULT, sorted unacknowledged-critical → unacknowledged-warning → acknowledged. ACKNOWLEDGING (the row collapses on touch-up, 200ms, anchored top; the tap is the receipt and the toast offers Undo). ACK FAILED (the row stands back up and the toast names it — an unacked alert never silently vanishes). ACKNOWLEDGED AND STILL LISTED (in All/Acknowledged the row renders at `ink2` with its mark intact and ' · acknowledged'; never a zero-height ghost). EMPTY ('Nothing to triage.' + 'Alerts appear here when a rule fires on a submitted visit.'). FILTERED EMPTY. LOADING / ERROR / OFFLINE (acknowledge queues and the row shows the held square). ALERT WITH NO VISIT (no 'View visit' at all — a link with nowhere to go is dishonest chrome). 2.0× (thumbnails drop, then actions move onto their own row).
items.behaviour: Rows enter with a 40ms cascade capped at eight. Acknowledge is idempotent, begins visibly on touch-up per the press model, and is guarded against a double-tap mid-collapse. Filter changes never refetch — filtering is client-side over the loaded page, so the list does not flash.
items.modes: Night as above. Day standard, press inverts. Veld: rows ~96dp, no thumbnails, one action per row (Acknowledge) as a 64dp block, the second moved into the detail.
items.accessibility: Rows announce severity, message, rule, outlet. Acknowledge is a real 44dp button. The optimistic collapse is announced via `liveRegion`. Nothing pinned at 2.0×.
items.amber: ONE — the nav pill's active block, as exempt chrome. This screen nominates no content amber at all, and under the revised ledger that costs nothing: the selected filter chip is `lifted` here exactly as it is everywhere else.
items.screenshot: A dark list screen: a small heading, a big crimson-outlined 7 with a triangle, a row of filter tablets with one filled slightly lighter, a faint rule reading 'Open 7', then bands each with a crimson bar, a sentence in off-white, a grey line with a monospaced rule code, a small thumbnail and two plain text actions.

items.name: Alert detail sheet
items.purpose: Everything behind one fired rule, without leaving the worklist.
items.anatomy: Bottom sheet, 80% max height, radius 14 top, `surface`, 1px `edgeStructure`, grabber, padding s5. (1) Severity mark plus word, then the message at `title.l`, max 3 lines. (2) s3, a `well` block at radius 6: 'OSA_BELOW_50 · threshold 50% · observed 34%' in `mono.ident`. (3) s5, the evidence photo at radius 10, full width, 16:9, with capture time and geotag in `mono.ident` beneath; absent entirely when there is none. (4) s5, a PERSON ROW for the submitting agent, name wrapping rather than truncating. (5) s3, flag chips. (6) s5, a 6-point trend of the offending metric with an `ink1` series. (7) s6, two stacked ghost controls: 'Acknowledge' and 'Open the visit'. Destructive actions do not live here.
items.states: DEFAULT, no-photo, no-visit (the control is absent, not disabled), already acknowledged (the control becomes a `raised` block naming who and when), loading, error (inline, inside the sheet, which does not close on failure), offline (actions queue with the held square), permission-limited (actions replaced by a line naming who can act, with their person row).
items.behaviour: Opens 320ms. Acknowledge closes the sheet first, then collapses the row behind it, so the manager sees the list update. Photo tap opens a full-screen viewer with pinch-zoom — the one place the raw, uncrushed image is shown.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: `surface` #FAF7F2 plus sh1. Veld: white, radius 0, 2px border, controls 64dp, the chart replaced by a three-row figure list.
items.accessibility: `scopesRoute`, focus to the message. The photo carries a real label naming outlet, section and time. Reading order: severity, message, rule, evidence, person, flags, trend summary, actions.
items.amber: None. The nav is behind the scrim and inert while a modal route owns the screen, and the sheet nominates nothing — its job is evidence, not direction.
items.screenshot: A dark panel risen over a list: a crimson triangle and the word Critical, a headline sentence, a monospaced rule line on a darker block, a photo of a half-empty shelf, a person row with initials, two outlined chips, a small chart, and two plain outlined buttons.

items.name: Alert rules
items.purpose: What raises the rows — visible and editable, one hop from the worklist.
items.anatomy: (1) Header `title.l` 'Alert rules' with a ghost 'Back to alerts'. (2) s6, a `meta` line: 'A rule evaluates on every visit submit. Turning one off stops new alerts; it does not clear existing ones.' (3) s8, SECTION RULE 'Active 6'. (4) Rule rows, 56dp min with 12dp gaps: name at `title.m`; beneath, the condition as a sentence with the metric and threshold in `mono.ident` — 'OSA_BELOW_50 · fires when on-shelf availability is under 50%'; trailing, a 44 × 28 toggle. Severity shows as a mark plus word at the left of the second line, never as the row's colour. (5) SECTION RULE 'Off 2' with the same rows at `ink2`. (6) A 44dp ghost 'New rule' at the bottom — not a FAB, which would collide with the nav circle.
items.states: Active / off. Toggling (optimistic, visible on touch-up; on failure it reverts and a toast names it). No threshold ('fires on any occurrence' rather than a null). Never fired (' · never fired' — useful, because a rule that never fires is usually mis-configured). Very noisy (' · 340 alerts in 7 days' with a half-filled triangle, because a noisy rule is a real problem). Empty ('No rules yet. Alerts only exist because a rule says so.'). Loading, error, offline (toggles disabled with the held square and one line). Role-limited (toggles replaced by the state as a word).
items.behaviour: Toggle 120ms with haptic. Editing pushes a form built from the Panel component — the one place on the console a Panel is legal, because a form is a form. No inline threshold editing in the list.
items.modes: Night as above. Day standard. Veld: rows ~96dp and toggles become two 64dp ON/OFF blocks, because a switch's thumb position is a small cue in sun.
items.accessibility: Each toggle is `Semantics(toggled:)` with the rule name in its label. The condition sentence is the accessible description, not the raw slug. At 2.0× the sentence wraps to three lines and the toggle moves beneath it.
items.amber: ONE — the nav pill, as exempt chrome. No nomination: a configuration list has nothing happening in it.
items.screenshot: A plain dark list of rules, each with a name, a grey sentence describing when it fires with a monospaced code in it, and a small switch at the right; a faint rule divides the active ones from the two that are off.

items.name: Tasks worklist
items.purpose: Open work with a clock on it, sorted by consequence.
items.anatomy: Same skeleton as Alerts. (1) Header plus 'Risks, stockouts and price deviations open a task automatically, with a due date set by priority.' (2) LEAD INDICATOR RAIL: OVERDUE is the dominant figure at `figure.l` with a filled triangle and a `bad` outline, because SLA is the axis that costs something; subordinate line '12 open · 4 awaiting verification'. (3) FILTER RAIL: Open · 12 / Overdue · 3 / Done / All, selected chip `lifted`. (4) SECTION RULE. (5) DECISION ROWS: the finding type as the title; the SLA in the reason in words, not a pill — 'Overdue by 2 days · replace the shelf talker' — with 'Overdue by' in `bad` behind a filled triangle; a thumbnail right where one exists; ghost actions 'Close with photo' and, once closed, 'Verify'. (6) Footer.
items.states: OPEN / OVERDUE (solid bar, filled triangle, the overdue phrasing) / DUE SOON under 24h (bar at 40%, half-filled triangle, 'Due in 6 h') / CLOSED (no bar, a `good` circle, 'Closed 24 Sep' plus Verify) / CLOSED AND VERIFIED (ink to `ink2`, 'Verified') / CLOSING (busy dots, row locked) / CLOSE FAILED (restored, toast with Retry) / NO VISIT LINKED (no 'Close with photo' at all — the closure photo uploads against a visit) / EMPTY ('Nothing outstanding.') / FILTERED EMPTY / LOADING / ERROR / OFFLINE (closures queue; the held square shows) / TOO MANY / 2.0×.
items.behaviour: Closing opens the close-with-photo sheet — no photo, no closure, and the button says so rather than failing afterwards. Verification is one tap with an Undo toast. Sort: overdue, critical, high, normal, closed. The clock is read ONCE per build and threaded down so every 'overdue' on the screen agrees.
items.modes: Night as above. Day standard. Veld: one action per row, rows ~96dp, the SLA phrase at 17/700, and 'Close with photo' as the one 64dp amber block when a single task is open in detail.
items.accessibility: 'Critical, overdue by 2 days, replace the shelf talker, Kasi Corner Spaza.' Overdue is a word, a triangle and a bar. Actions ≥ 44; at 2.0× they stack beneath the reason.
items.amber: ONE — the nav pill, as exempt chrome; no content nomination. The overdue lead figure and the SLA phrasing carry the urgency, and the earlier draft's reasoning that the filter chip should be lit 'because a slot was free' no longer exists as a possibility.
items.screenshot: A dark list with a big crimson-outlined 3 and a triangle at the top, filter tablets below, then rows headed by findings like 'Shelf talker missing', each with a crimson triangle and 'Overdue by 2 days' in the grey line, a small photo at the right, and 'Close with photo'.

items.name: Close-with-photo sheet
items.purpose: The closure gate: evidence, or the task stays open.
items.anatomy: Bottom sheet, `surface`, radius 14 top, 1px `edgeStructure`, grabber, padding s5. (1) 'Close this task' at `title.l`. (2) s3, the required fix at `body` `ink2`. (3) s5, the capture field: a 96dp pre-capture card, radius 10, 1px `edgeControl`, holding a 2px-stroke framing drawing, the instruction ('Photograph the fix so a manager can see it, not take your word for it') and a reminder at `meta` ('Switch the phone torch on in a dark aisle'). Below, a 44dp ghost 'Take a photo' handing off to the OS camera — Phase 1 ships no in-app preview and this screen does not pretend otherwise. (4) On return: a 72dp thumbnail at radius 10 with capture time and geotag in `mono.ident`, plus a ghost 'Retake'. (5) s6: 'Close task' (44dp, `lifted` + 1px `flame600` rim + 2px bleed) and a ghost 'Cancel'.
items.states: NO PHOTO (Close disabled: `well`, `inkMute`, NO rim, and 'A photo is required' beneath — disabled rather than hidden, so the reason is visible). PHOTO TAKEN. DARK PHOTO (mean luma < 18%: a 2px `comparisonWash` edge and 'Dark frame — mean brightness 11%. Retake?' — the measurement, never the cause; it is never auto-rejected, because during Stage 6 the dark photo may be the only evidence there is). NO GEOTAG ('No location — the closure will record without one'; it still goes ahead). UPLOADING (busy dots from touch-up, Cancel disabled). UPLOAD FAILED (the sheet stays open, the photo is retained, inline error with Retry — the photo is never lost). OFFLINE ('Hold and send later'). CANCELLED (the task stays open, which is correct).
items.behaviour: Opens 320ms. Close routes through no confirm sheet — closing is reversible by reopening, and a second confirm on routine work trains people to tap through confirms. The sheet closes on success with a receipt and an Undo.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: Close is a solid `flame600` block with `onAmber` ink. Veld: 64dp controls, a 2px-bordered pre-capture card, Close a solid amber block with `veld-ink` that inverts to the ink block on press.
items.accessibility: `scopesRoute`, focus to the title. The disabled Close announces its reason. The thumbnail carries a label naming the task and capture time. Controls ≥ 44 (64 in Veld).
items.amber: ONE nomination — the Close button's rim (a block in Day and Veld). Plus the nav pill behind the scrim, inert.
items.screenshot: A dark panel with a heading, a grey sentence describing the fix, a tall outlined card with a line drawing and the instruction to photograph it, then a wide dark button with a warm amber outline reading 'Close task' and a plain Cancel.

items.name: Territories list
items.purpose: Which territories exist, how covered they are, and which one is hurting.
items.anatomy: (1) Header plus 'A territory groups outlets and the agents who work them.' (2) s6, LEAD INDICATOR RAIL: the worst territory's coverage as the dominant figure with its name at `label` above. (3) s8, SECTION RULE '6 territories'. (4) RANKED BAR ROWS, worst-first — the one console list where the ranked bar IS the row: name left (middle-truncated), a 6px coverage track, value right at `figure.s`, and beneath each at `meta`: '34 outlets · 4 agents · 8 not visited this window'. Rows 56dp min with 12dp gaps. (5) A 44dp ghost 'New territory' at the bottom. (6) Footer if truncated.
items.states: DEFAULT. NO COVERAGE DATA for a territory (track drawn, no fill, the hatch mark at the label's left, em dash value, and 'not measured — no visits in this window' — never a zero bar, which reads as total failure). NO TERRITORIES ('No territories yet. Create one to group outlets and assign agents.'). TERRITORIES BUT NO SCORES ('6 territories, none scored yet. Scores appear after the first submitted visit.' — a settled answer, never a loader). LOADING / ERROR / OFFLINE. ROLE-LIMITED. ONE TERRITORY (the ranked bar degrades to a single figure block and the lead rail is removed — a ranking of one is not a ranking). TOO MANY (8 bars plus footer). 2.0× (name above its own track, two-line rows).
items.behaviour: Bars draw in once over 320ms on one controller with a 40ms stagger. Row tap pushes the territory. Long-press does nothing.
items.modes: Night: this screen NOMINATES the worst territory's bar as its content amber — `flame600` fill, bloom, origin triangle, bolder label. Day and Veld: focus is `ink1` fill plus marker plus weight.
items.accessibility: 'Gauteng North, coverage 61 percent, worst of six, 34 outlets, 4 agents, 8 not visited.' 'Worst' is stated in words so the focus channel is never only visual. Rows ≥ 56.
items.amber: TWO, counted: the nav pill (exempt chrome) and the single nominated focus bar. Nothing else on the screen can become amber, because no component here defaults to lit.
items.screenshot: A dark screen with a stack of labelled horizontal bars, worst at the top — the top bar glowing warm amber with a small triangle at its left end and a bolder name, the rest flat warm grey — each with a small grey line counting outlets and agents.

items.name: Territory view
items.purpose: One territory: how it is performing, where its outlets are, and who works it.
items.anatomy: (1) Header: territory name at `title.l`, code in `mono.ident` beneath. (2) s6, a 2×2 STAT CLUSTER separated by 16/20dp ground gutters and no lines: coverage, OSA, outlets visited, agents active. (3) s8, SECTION RULE 'Where'. (4) REVISED: a 260dp MAP PREVIEW at radius 14 that is NON-INTERACTIVE — a static camera, outlet dots as 10px hollow-centre navy discs, agent positions as state glyphs, no polylines, and a 44dp 'Open the map' ghost beneath it alongside '4 on the map · 2 not checked in today.' One-finger drag over a preview scrolls the page, which is what a thumb in the middle of a scrolling screen is doing; the old embedded map swallowed the gesture, panned off Gauteng and left the page stuck. The real map lives on its own route where it owns every gesture. (5) s8, SECTION RULE 'Not visited 8' with decision rows carrying days-since at `figure.m` and, where one exists, the agent's skip reason (#395): 'Skipped 22 Sep — store refused'. (6) s8, SECTION RULE 'Who' with person rows, each with a held-work row beneath when work is held. (7) Ghost actions: 'Edit territory', 'Assign agents'.
items.states: DEFAULT. NO OUTLETS ('No outlets in this territory yet.' plus a ghost; the preview is not rendered, because a grey empty map looks broken rather than honest). OUTLETS BUT NO CHECK-INS (the base layer renders and the footer says so — a store network is worth showing on a quiet morning). TILES FAILED (the preview becomes an inline error with Retry; the list beneath is unaffected). NO AGENTS ASSIGNED. SKIP REASON ABSENT ('Not visited in 14 days' with no invented reason). LOADING / ERROR PER REGION / OFFLINE (cached tiles, greyed, 'Tiles are from your last connection'). 2.0× (the preview holds 260dp; everything else grows).
items.behaviour: The preview's camera is computed by the app's own Mercator fit from the measured widget size and handed over as a plain centre and zoom — never via the map library's camera fit, which races. A filter change eases the same camera over 320ms rather than snapping. REVISED tint: the navy is a `ColorFilter` applied to each tile image as it is decoded and cached, not a colour layer over the widget — a saveLayer over a panning raster was the one place this document let a layer in, and it would have stuttered at 20–30fps on a Mali-G51.
items.modes: Night: tiles tinted navy at decode, markers drawn untinted above. Day: no tint. Veld: no map at all — an outlet list with distances; a tinted raster at 40% backlight in sun is unreadable and costs the bundle for nothing.
items.accessibility: The preview is `Semantics(label: '4 agents and 34 outlets in Gauteng North', excludeSemantics: true)` and the same information is in the list beneath — the map is never the only route to its data. Every pin has a label. Sections are headers.
items.amber: ONE — the nav pill, as exempt chrome. The map carries none: 'you are here' is an ink disc with a white ring, because amber leaves the map entirely.
items.screenshot: A dark screen with four unboxed stat cells in a clean grid, then a navy-tinted map image with small hollow dots and an 'Open the map' link beneath it, then a faint rule reading 'Not visited 8' over rows of outlets with day counts, then 'Who' over rows of people with initials.

items.name: Territory health decomposition sheet
items.purpose: Makes the hero number decomposable, because a composite score nobody can take apart is a number you cannot act on.
items.anatomy: Bottom sheet, `surface`, radius 14 top, 1px `edgeStructure`, grabber, padding s5. (1) 'Territory health' at `label` `ink2`, then the composite at `hero.figure.compact` 56/600 with its delta on the same baseline. (2) s3, 'Four weighted inputs, measured over the last 30 days.' (3) s6, four INPUT ROWS at 72dp with 12dp gaps: name at `title.m`; weight at `meta` ('×0.30'); the value at `figure.m` tabular mono right; and a 6px contribution bar beneath — `lifted` track, `chartNeutral` fill. The input that moved the score most takes `ink1` fill, a filled triangle at the bar's origin and a `body.strong` label — focus without amber. (4) s6, one `meta` line: 'Weights are set in Scoring config. Last recomputed 03:10.'
items.states: DEFAULT. UNMEASURED INPUT (em dash at `figure.m` in `ink3`, the bar HATCHED at the revised `ink3` 4dp-period / 2px-stroke setting, and the words "can't confirm — 2 of 14 outlets unvisited" — the old `inkMute`-on-`lifted` hatch at 1.77:1 and a 2dp period averaged to a flat grey bar on a 1x panel, i.e. to the zero bar it exists to not be, and a manager would have coached an agent about a dimension nobody measured). PROVISIONAL COMPOSITE (dotted rule, the word, and the reconciliation line in the console's third-person voice). WEIGHTS NOT CONFIGURED (all four show '×—' plus a `bad`-outlined note: 'No weights are set. This score is an unweighted mean.'). ONE INPUT ONLY (no focus treatment — a focus of one is not a focus). LOADING / ERROR inside the sheet.
items.behaviour: Opens 320ms. No count-up anywhere, here or on the plate. Tapping an input row pushes that metric's trend.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: hatch `ink3` #676052 on `well` #E2DBCC (4.52:1), focus fill `ink1`. Veld: rows ~96dp, bars 12px with 2px borders, hatch at a 3dp period, and the focus input additionally marked with the words 'largest change'.
items.accessibility: 'Territory health 72, down 19. Four inputs. On-shelf availability, weight 0.30, 61 percent, largest change. Price compliance, weight 0.20, cannot confirm, 2 of 14 outlets unvisited.' Hatch is announced as "can't confirm", never as a value, and never renders without those words. Rows ≥ 72.
items.amber: None. A decomposition is analysis, and the one light on the screen behind it is already pointed at the shelf.
items.screenshot: A dark panel with a large 72 and a crimson −19, then four rows each with a name, a small '×0.30', a mono value and a thin bar — one bar in bright off-white with a triangle at its start, one filled with coarse pale diagonal stripes and a long dash instead of a number.

items.name: Agent scorecard / coaching view
items.purpose: One agent, honestly: what they did, what got in their way, and what to say to them.
items.anatomy: (1) PERSON ROW at the top, enlarged: a 56dp identity tile, the full name at `title.l` wrapping to two lines, 'Field agent · Gauteng North · since Mar 2025', and the agent reference in `mono.ident`. (2) s6, HELD-WORK ROW when work is held — placed HIGH on purpose, because a quiet scorecard caused by a dead tower is not a performance problem. (3) s6, a 2×2 STAT CLUSTER in ground gutters: visits submitted, average score, tasks closed, on-time rate, each using the no-data variant when the window is empty. (4) s8, 'Score over time' plus the trend chart — this agent solid `ink1`, the territory median dashed `comparison`, the target dashed, legend mandatory. (5) s8, 'Where it went wrong 4' plus decision rows naming the dimension, the figure and the worst outlet, with unmeasured dimensions carrying the hatch mark and its words. (6) s8, 'Flags 2' plus flag chips, each tappable into its evidence. (7) s8, 'Progress' plus progress bars with `ink2` ticks. (8) s8, 'Today' plus a 44dp row into the day trail. (9) Ghost actions: 'Raise a coaching task', 'Message'.
items.states: DEFAULT. NEW AGENT ('Joined 4 days ago. Two visits submitted — not enough to score.'; every tile no-data; no chart, replaced by one line). NO VISITS IN WINDOW (em dashes plus a ghost 'Widen to 90 days'). DEACTIVATED (a `comparison` square and 'Deactivated 12 Sep'; actions removed, history readable). ALL FLAGS CLEARED (the section renders with 'Two flags, both cleared' rather than disappearing). HELD WORK STUCK (the `bad` edge and 'Message the agent'). PROVISIONAL SCORE (dotted rule and the reconciliation line). LOADING / ERROR PER REGION / OFFLINE. ROLE-LIMITED (a peer manager sees the person row and 'This agent works Gauteng South. Ask Nomsa D. for their scorecard.' plus her person row — never a blank 403). 2.0×.
items.behaviour: Sections enter with a 40ms stagger capped at four; the trend draws once at 320ms. 'Raise a coaching task' opens the task form pre-filled with the worst dimension and this agent as assignee — the coaching action is the point of the screen, so it is not a generic create.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: chart focus and comparison per the light-ground rules. Veld: the chart becomes a four-row figure list ('This month 71 · Last month 78 · Territory median 74 · Target 75'), flags as 56dp bordered chips, and one amber commit block ('Raise a coaching task').
items.accessibility: Reading order: person, held work, figures, trend summary sentence, worst dimensions severity-first, flags, progress, actions. The chart's semantics carry a written summary. Sections are headers; actions ≥ 44.
items.amber: ONE — the nav pill, as exempt chrome. No nomination in Night: the manager is reading, not being pointed. Veld nominates the coaching commit, because Veld always has exactly one block.
items.screenshot: A dark screen headed by initials and a full name over two lines, a warm-brown-marked band reading '4 visits held on this phone', four unboxed stat cells, a small chart with a solid and a dashed curve and a two-item legend, then faint rules over weak dimensions, two outlined flag chips, and a slim progress bar.

items.name: Agent day trail
items.purpose: One agent's day as it actually happened — stops, order, gaps.
items.anatomy: REVISED to list-first. (1) Header: the agent's name and a 44dp date control showing the day in `mono.ident`. (2) A 200dp NON-INTERACTIVE MAP PREVIEW at radius 14: numbered pins (the ordinal at `figure.s` on a `raised` disc), a 2px `chartNeutral` polyline in time order, the last stop in the agent's state glyph, live position as a distinct square when the day is today; beneath it a 44dp ghost 'Open the map'. (3) STOP ROWS at 64dp with 12dp gaps: ordinal, outlet at `title.m`, check-in time in `mono.ident`, duration, and flag chips where the stop was out of fence or the visit unfinished. (4) A `meta` legend line naming what the polyline is and is not: 'A line between confirmed check-ins. It is not a travelled route.' The FULL-SCREEN MAP is its own route where the map owns every gesture and the stops become a bottom sheet — the old 55%-height map called itself full-screen, kept wheel zoom and sat above a scrollable list, which is the same gesture collision the territory view had.
items.states: DEFAULT. NO CHECK-INS ('No check-ins on this day.' plus the date control; no preview rendered). TODAY, IN PROGRESS (the last pin pulses — the one motion-coded semantic amber in the product). GAP (a stop pair more than 3 hours apart gets a 44dp interstitial: '3 h 20 m gap' with a `comparison` square — a fact, not an accusation). OUT-OF-FENCE STOP (chip with the measured distance). UNFINISHED VISIT (chip, and the duration reads 'not submitted'). LIVE POSITION UNAVAILABLE ('Last seen 11:48' rather than a stale pin at a confident position). TILES FAILED / OFFLINE. FUTURE DATE ('That day has not happened yet.').
items.behaviour: REVISED pulse: 3200ms, Night only, capped at 60 seconds and then falling to the static filled square plus the word 'Live' — the same degradation it already used for reduced motion — and stopped on app-background and battery saver via the shared Ticker. It animates the opacity of one pre-baked gradient Picture, never a per-frame shader. Without the cap, the one screen a manager parks on her desk repainted a halo over a tinted raster for twenty minutes with GPS polling behind it. Tapping a pin opens the full map at that stop; tapping a row scrolls the preview's cached camera to it.
items.modes: Night: navy tint applied per tile at decode, polyline `chartNeutral`. Day: no tint, polyline `ink1`. Veld: no map at all — the stop list alone at ~96dp rows with 2px borders and distances printed as figures.
items.accessibility: The list is the accessible equivalent and is always present. Pins carry ordinal-and-outlet labels. The pulse announces as the word 'Live'. Date control ≥ 44.
items.amber: TWO, counted: the nav pill (exempt chrome) and the nominated live pulse, which exists only when the day is today and a visit is genuinely in progress. On any past date the screen nominates nothing. The nav no longer goes dark to make room, which was the substitution that would have read as a bug.
items.screenshot: A dark screen with a map image at the top showing numbered discs joined by a grey line, the last disc breathing with a soft amber halo, an 'Open the map' link beneath it, and a list of stops with monospaced times and one outlined chip reading 'Out of fence · 140 m'.

items.name: Fraud review queue
items.purpose: Visits the engine thinks may be faked, riskiest first, with the evidence in the row rather than behind it.
items.anatomy: (1) Header plus 'Risk is scored 0–100 on submit. The signals are the evidence.' (2) s6, LEAD INDICATOR RAIL: the high-risk count at `figure.l` with a filled triangle and a `bad` outline; '9 elevated · 41 low risk'. (3) s3, the UNSCORED NOTE where applicable: '6 submitted visits have not been scored yet and are not listed here.' (4) s6, FILTER RAIL: risk band and territory. (5) s8, SECTION RULE. (6) CASE ROWS, 88dp min with 12dp gaps: a person row's identity tile and the agent's FULL name as the title, WRAPPING to two lines and never truncated — on a 360dp row with a tile, a thumbnail and a bar, 'Nomsa Dlamini-Mkhize' and 'Nomsa Dlamini-Ndlovu' truncated to the same string, and no accusation is recorded against a name the manager could not read; beneath, outlet and check-in time; then the risk at `figure.m` with its band word ('Risk 84 · High risk') and the fired codes in `mono.ident`; then the signals' detail on one `body` line; flag chips; a 40dp thumbnail right. A 3px `bad` bar for high risk, 40% for elevated, none for low. (7) Footer with the true page size.
items.states: DEFAULT, riskiest first. NOTHING FLAGGED ('Nothing flagged. Visits appear here when the engine scores one above the review threshold.'). NOTHING FLAGGED BUT UNSCORED EXIST (the same empty state PLUS the unscored note — the two facts must not merge, and this is exactly where a clean-looking empty state would be a lie). ALREADY REVIEWED (ink to `ink2`, the verdict as a word with its mark, moved below the unreviewed). BEING REVIEWED BY SOMEONE ELSE ('Being reviewed by Thabo M. since 14:02' with a `comparison` square; openable read-only). AGENT UNRESOLVABLE (the person row's unknown state — never a UUID as a title). NO THUMBNAIL. LOADING / ERROR / OFFLINE (verdicts queue; the held square shows). TOO MANY. 2.0× (thumbnail drops, codes wrap, the row passes 160dp as the name takes two lines).
items.behaviour: Row tap pushes the case. No inline verdict — accusing someone of faking a visit is never a one-tap action in a list. Cascade capped at eight rows.
items.modes: Night as above. Day standard. Veld: rendered at Veld density with no thumbnails and one action, and a `meta` line saying review is better done sitting down. I hold on that line against the critique's discomfort: the alternative is an escalation recorded in a forecourt at 40% backlight, and an honest refusal beats a degraded surface pretending to be equivalent.
items.accessibility: 'High risk, 84. Nomsa Dlamini-Mkhize, Kasi Corner Spaza, checked in 09:12. Signals: GPS mismatch, duplicate photo.' Severity first, person second, never an id. The full name is in the semantics regardless of paint. Rows ≥ 88.
items.amber: ONE — the nav pill, as exempt chrome. No nomination: nothing on an accusation screen should be lit like an invitation.
items.screenshot: A dark list where each band starts with a crimson bar, shows initials and a full name over two lines, the outlet and time beneath, a mono 'Risk 84 · High risk' with rule codes, a grey sentence of detail, and a small photo at the right.

items.name: Fraud case and verdict
items.purpose: One flagged visit, all its evidence, and the control that records what the manager decided.
items.anatomy: (1) PERSON ROW for the agent, enlarged, full name wrapping, with a ghost 'Open their scorecard'. (2) s6, a `well` block at radius 6: visit reference in `mono.ident`, outlet, check-in and submit times, duration. (3) s6, the RISK FIGURE at `figure.l` with its band word and a filled triangle — never a gauge, never a dial. (4) s6, SECTION RULE 'Signals 3' plus one 72dp row per signal: the code in `mono.ident`, the human sentence at `body` `ink1`, the measured evidence at `figure.s` ('check-in was 1.4 km from the outlet'), and a ghost opening that signal's own evidence. (5) s8, 'What the agent captured' plus a 72dp photo strip at radius 10, horizontally scrollable, each thumb opening a full viewer; dark frames carry the `comparisonWash` edge and the measured caption 'Dark frame — mean brightness 11%', never a supplied excuse. (6) s8, 'How this compares' plus a ranked bar of this agent's risk against their own last ten visits, focus on THIS visit in `ink1`. (7) s8, the VERDICT CONTROL. (8) s6, a history block of prior verdicts, each with the manager's person row and timestamp.
items.states: DEFAULT. NO PHOTOS ('No photos were captured on this visit.' — itself a signal, and stated rather than an empty strip). SIGNAL WITH NO EVIDENCE LINK (the ghost is absent, not disabled). ALREADY DECIDED (the committed block with 'Change this verdict' for 24 hours, then a lock line). DECIDED BY SOMEONE ELSE WHILE OPEN (committed block plus a `bad`-edged note, the manager's unsaved selection preserved in words). ESCALATED (a `badSolid` block at the top: 'Escalated to investigation 24 Sep. This visit is locked.'). AGENT DEACTIVATED SINCE (a `comparison` note; verdicts still recordable). LOADING / ERROR / OFFLINE (records locally with the held square). 2.0× (signal rows grow to three lines; the strip keeps 72dp thumbs and scrolls).
items.behaviour: Escalate routes through the confirm sheet; clear and coach do not. The commit shows its busy state on touch-up. On commit the screen does not navigate away — it replaces the control in place so the manager sees the record she just made. The photo viewer shows the raw uncrushed image.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: the commit is the solid amber block; ranked focus `ink1`. Veld: signals as ~96dp bordered rows, the photo strip reduced to a count and a ghost ('4 photos — open'), commit a 64dp amber block.
items.accessibility: Reading order: agent, visit facts, risk band, each signal with its measurement, photo count, comparison summary, the verdict control as a radio group, history. The risk figure is announced with its band word. Nothing about the decision is encoded in colour alone.
items.amber: TWO, counted: the nav pill (exempt chrome) and the nominated verdict commit. On the most consequential screen in the product the single content light is on the decision — and under the revised ledger it gets there without the nav having to go dark.
items.screenshot: A dark screen with a person's row at the top, a monospaced visit reference on a darker block, a large mono 84 with a crimson triangle and 'High risk', three rows naming signals and what they measured, a strip of small dark photos, a short bar chart, and three tall outlined verdict rows with a warm-amber-outlined 'Record verdict' beneath.

items.name: Reports
items.purpose: Saved definitions a manager can run against live data, and see the size of what came back.
items.anatomy: (1) Header plus a ghost 'Schedules'. (2) s6, 'Definitions run on demand against live data.' (3) s8, SECTION RULE '7 reports'. (4) REPORT ROWS, 56dp min with 12dp gaps: name at `title.m`; beneath, the type slug in `mono.ident` — machine-facing, so a manager can quote it back into a definition — plus, once run this session, the row count ('outlet_coverage · 1 284 rows'); trailing ghosts 'Run' and 'Delete'. A state mark sits at the left of the second line: a `good` circle and 'Generated' once run, an `ink3` square and 'Ready' before. (5) A 44dp ghost 'New report' at the bottom.
items.states: READY / RUNNING (three travelling `ink2` dots on the Run action from touch-up, never a spinner; the row locks) / GENERATED / RETURNED ZERO ROWS (a `comparison` square and '0 rows — the query matched nothing'; zero is a real answer and is never suppressed or shown as an error) / FAILED ('Could not run' with a half-filled triangle and Retry, the previous count retained) / TIMED OUT ('Still running after 60 s. It will finish server-side; check Run history.') / DELETING (confirm sheet first — a saved definition someone else uses is not a one-tap delete) / EMPTY ('No saved reports. Build one, then run it to see how many rows it returns.') / LOADING / OFFLINE (Run disabled with 'A report runs on the server. This needs a connection.' — the one place the console admits a hard dependency rather than queueing) / ROLE-LIMITED.
items.behaviour: Run is optimistic in its busy state only, never in its result. A completed run pushes the result screen rather than only updating the row — a manager who ran a report wants to see it. Delete confirms.
items.modes: Night as above. Day standard. Veld: rows ~96dp, one action per row (Run), Delete moved into the report's detail.
items.accessibility: 'Outlet coverage, outlet_coverage, generated, 1 284 rows. Run button. Delete button.' State is mark plus word. Actions ≥ 44.
items.amber: ONE — the nav pill, as exempt chrome. No nomination.
items.screenshot: A plain dark list of report names, each with a monospaced slug and row count beneath and two plain text actions at the right; one row shows three small dots travelling where 'Run' was.

items.name: Report run result
items.purpose: What the report actually returned, at a size a phone can hold.
items.anatomy: (1) Header: report name at `title.l`, and beneath at `meta` the slug in `mono.ident`, the run time and the row count. (2) s6, a 2×2 STAT CLUSTER in ground gutters where the report type defines one — rows, outlets covered, period, generated at; figures over 5 glyphs step down the `figure.l` → `figure.m` → FittedBox ladder, which is why '1 284' no longer clips a 160dp cell. (3) s8, SECTION RULE 'Rows 1 284'. (4) PHONE (<900dp): each row is a stacked block, 88dp min with 12dp gaps — the primary identifier at `title.m`, two or three key figures beneath as label/figure pairs in a Wrap, and a chevron into the record. A table is not forced onto 360dp. (5) ≥900dp: a real table — header row at `eyebrow` on a `well` band, rows 44dp, figures right-aligned in tabular mono, the whole table in its own horizontally scrollable box so the page never scrolls sideways. (6) A ghost 'Export CSV' and a `meta` line naming the export's row cap.
items.states: DEFAULT. ZERO ROWS ('The query matched nothing in this window.' plus the parameters used, in `mono.ident`). TRUNCATED ('Showing the first 500 of 1 284 rows. Export for the rest.'). RUNNING (skeleton). FAILED (inline error with the parameters shown). PARTIAL COLUMNS (a column the backend did not return is omitted from the header rather than showing empty cells). NULL CELL (em dash in `ink3`, never blank — a blank cell is indistinguishable from a rendering bug). VERY LONG CELL (middle-truncated, full value in the record). EXPORTING (busy dots). 2.0× (the table collapses to stacked blocks regardless of width, because a 2.0× table is not a table).
items.behaviour: Horizontal scroll is contained; the page scrolls vertically only. Column widths compute once from the first 50 rows and then fix, so scrolling does not reflow. No sorting on phone; at ≥900dp a header tap sorts with a 12px triangle showing direction.
items.modes: Night as above. Day standard. Veld: no table ever, stacked blocks at ~96dp with 2px borders and a `meta` line: 'Large results are easier to read indoors.'
items.accessibility: A real semantics table with row and column headers at ≥900dp; the stacked form is a list of labelled figure pairs. Sort direction is a triangle plus an announced word. Every figure is tabular mono.
items.amber: ONE — the nav pill, as exempt chrome. Nothing in a result set is lit.
items.screenshot: A dark screen with four small stat cells in clear gutters, a faint rule reading 'Rows 1 284', then stacked blocks each with an outlet name and two or three small label-and-number pairs.

items.name: Report schedules
items.purpose: Which reports run on their own, when, and to whom.
items.anatomy: (1) Header plus a ghost 'Back to reports'. (2) s6, 'A schedule runs its report server-side and emails the result.' (3) s8, SECTION RULE 'Active 3'. (4) SCHEDULE ROWS, 64dp with 12dp gaps: report name at `title.m`; beneath, the cadence in words plus the next run in `mono.ident` — 'Every Monday 06:00 · next 22 Sep 06:00'; beneath that, recipients as a count with a ghost expanding them into person rows; trailing, a 44 × 28 toggle. (5) SECTION RULE 'Off 1'. (6) SECTION RULE 'Last runs' plus 56dp history rows: timestamp in `mono.ident`, outcome as a mark plus word ('Delivered' with a `good` circle / 'Failed' with a `bad` triangle / 'Skipped — no rows' with a `comparison` square), and the row count.
items.states: ACTIVE / OFF / NEVER RUN ('Scheduled, not yet run') / LAST RUN FAILED (the schedule row itself gains a half-filled triangle and 'Last run failed 15 Sep' — a schedule quietly failing is the worst thing this screen could hide) / RECIPIENT LIST EMPTY (a `bad` outline and 'No recipients — this schedule delivers to nobody', because that is almost certainly a mistake) / PAUSED BY THE SYSTEM after three consecutive failures (a `badSolid` note and a ghost 'Resume') / EMPTY ('No schedules. A report runs on demand until you schedule it.') / LOADING / ERROR / OFFLINE (toggles disabled with one line).
items.behaviour: Toggling is optimistic from touch-up with a revert on failure. Expanding recipients animates 200ms. Editing pushes the schedule form — a Panel, legitimately, because it is a form.
items.modes: Night as above. Day standard. Veld: rows ~96dp, toggles as two 64dp ON/OFF blocks.
items.accessibility: 'Outlet coverage, every Monday at 6, next run 22 September, 4 recipients, active.' Outcome marks are silhouette plus word. Toggles are `Semantics(toggled:)`. At 2.0× the cadence wraps and the toggle moves beneath it.
items.amber: ONE — the nav pill, as exempt chrome.
items.screenshot: A dark list of schedules, each with a report name, a grey line of cadence and next run in monospaced type, a recipients count and a switch; below, a faint rule over a short history marked with small green circles and one crimson triangle.

items.name: Session ended (#392, console)
items.purpose: A state, not an error — and it shows the work that is still here.
items.anatomy: The console stays rendered behind at full fidelity under a 72% scrim — the manager can see her dashboard, which is the point. A `surface` sheet rises from the bottom, radius 14 top, 1px `edgeStructure`, no grabber (not dismissible), padding s5. (1) 'Your session ended at 16:20.' at `title.l` with the time in `mono.ident`. (2) s3, 'Nothing was lost.' (3) Where drafts exist, s5 and a `well` block listing each — the draft in words plus its record in `mono.ident` ('Your verdict on VS-8841, unsent') with a 10px `comparison` square. (4) s6, the primary: 'Sign in again', full width, 44dp, `lifted` + 1px `flame600` rim + 2px bleed. (5) s2, a ghost 'Show me what's held'. (6) s5, 'You will come back to this screen.'
items.states: NO DRAFTS (the block is absent and the body reads 'Nothing was lost — the console had nothing unsent.'). WITH DRAFTS (listed, counted in the headline beyond three). EXPIRED VS REVOKED (revoked reads 'Your access to this account was changed at 16:20' with the account owner's person row and NO 'Sign in again', because signing in again would fail and a button that cannot work is worse than none). NETWORK-INDUCED (this screen is not shown at all; the offline banner is, because an offline console is not a signed-out console — conflating them was the bug). SIGNING IN (busy dots). SIGN-IN FAILED (inline error inside the sheet; drafts still listed). SIGNED IN AGAIN (200ms exit, and the router returns to the exact same route, scroll offset and filter — never to the dashboard root).
items.behaviour: Not dismissible by scrim, drag or back; the content behind is inert. Drafts live in local storage and survive the app being killed; the ghost lists them without requiring sign-in, because a manager should be able to see that her work exists before she can prove who she is.
items.modes: Night as above. Day: `surface` #FAF7F2 plus sh1, the primary a solid amber block. Veld: white sheet, 2px border, a 64dp amber block, and a flat 72% overlay rather than a scrim fade.
items.accessibility: `scopesRoute`, announced as a dialog, focus to the headline. The draft list is a real list announced in words, never as a code alone. The primary announces what happens after sign-in ('returns you to the fraud queue'). Controls ≥ 44.
items.amber: TWO by the letter, one in practice: the nominated 'Sign in again' rim, plus the nav pill behind the scrim — which renders at `inkMute` for the duration, not to satisfy the ledger but because it is genuinely inert and must look it.
items.screenshot: A dimmed dashboard behind a dark panel reading 'Your session ended at 16:20' with a monospaced time, a small block listing one unsent verdict with a warm-brown square, a wide button with a warm amber outline, and a plain 'Show me what's held' beneath.

items.name: Tablet and desktop widths
items.purpose: What changes above a phone, stated as rules rather than left to a grid.
items.anatomy: THREE BREAKPOINTS, all on LayoutBuilder width, never on a text-scale guess. <600dp (the design case): one column, gutter s5, floating pill plus circle, the plate at its fold-budget height, stat cluster 2×2 in 16/20 ground gutters, no chart tooltips, and no 40dp of deliberate nothing. 600–1079dp: gutter s5; The Floor goes two-up beneath the plate — the decision list at flex 19 and an instrument column (lead indicator rail, stat cluster, coverage) at flex 10; the 40dp of nothing returns above the first section rule, where there is room for it; the plate becomes 21:9 capped at 320; charts gain axis labels and a second series; worklists stay single-column, because two columns destroy the worst-first reading order. ≥1080dp: gutter s8; the pill is REPLACED by a persistent 240dp left rail — `well` fill, 1px `edgeStructure` right edge, three verb groups at `eyebrow`, rows 44dp, active row `lifted` + a 3px `flame600` left bar + weight 700; the primary circle becomes a 44dp labelled button at the top of the rail; the plate spans the content area, not the viewport; tables become real tables; charts gain hover tooltips. Content never exceeds 1200dp of column width — beyond that the right side is left empty rather than stretching a 76dp row to 1600dp.
items.states: Each breakpoint keeps its full state set; responsive rules change layout, never content. Resize re-lays out without animation and without remounting a map (which would snap the camera). Split-screen and foldables: width alone decides; height never selects a layout, though it still drives the plate's fold budget.
items.behaviour: No horizontal page scroll at any width; tables and wide charts each get their own overflow box. The nav swap at 1080 is a layout change, not a route change — state and scroll survive it.
items.modes: All three skins honour all three breakpoints, except Veld, which is phone-only by construction (`TiqSkin.veld()` takes no density argument, so Veld × Console cannot be built).
items.accessibility: The rail at ≥1080 is a real navigation landmark with the groups as headers. Keyboard focus order follows visual order at every width. The 2.0× rule sits ABOVE the breakpoints: at 2.0× the two-up collapses back to one column regardless of width, because two columns of 28px body text on a 900dp tablet is two columns of four words.
items.amber: One at every width — the active nav slot, as the pill's block on phone and the rail's 3px left bar on desktop, exempt chrome in both cases. The screen's single nomination is unchanged by the viewport.
items.screenshot: Three frames side by side: a phone with a floating dark bar and one amber block; a tablet with the decision list left and the figures stacked right; a desktop with a dark sidebar whose active row carries a short amber bar at its left edge.

items.name: A manager outdoors (Veld × Field)
items.purpose: What the console becomes when a regional manager opens it in a forecourt at midday — and what it honestly refuses to become.
items.anatomy: A third theme, not a contrast tweak: ground pure white, ink #0E141A (18.52:1), secondary #4A4437 (9.66:1), every hairline a 2px #1B2632 border, every shadow, gradient, rim, blur and glow removed rather than softened. Type steps by declared members: body 15→17, label 13→16, meta 12→14, title.m 16→18, figure.m 22→24, a 600 weight floor, line-height +0.05, tracking +0.5% (and the eyebrow's own tracking drops to +4% as it does everywhere). Gutter s6 = 24, rows 64, targets 56, block gap s8 = 40. Density halves, and that is correct: precision is what you lose outdoors, not patience. REVISED: the nav DOCKS — full-bleed, 72dp, a 2px top border — because a white pill floating 20dp above white rows under glare stopped reading as a bar, and docking returns 36dp of fold to a skin that spends 64dp on a row. WHAT THE CONSOLE DROPS OUTDOORS: the plate, every sparkline, every trend chart (a four-row figure list instead), the territory map (an outlet list with distances), the report table, and the fraud queue's thumbnails. WHAT IT KEEPS: the hero figure, the lead indicator, three decision rows, the held-work row, flag chips, the person row, the progress bar with a printed percentage, and exactly one commit action.
items.states: Entered by the 56dp skin cycle (the only load-bearing mechanism), by solar elevation computed from the last GPS fix and the device clock gated on a STATE CHANGE — crossing 35° or arriving somewhere new — cross-checked against GPS accuracy and last-capture luma, never on a standing condition, and by memory of the last choice at this place and hour. It does NOT auto-expire: glance-work-glance was exactly the pattern that reverted the only readable screen while the manager was still in the sun. It exits on the skin cycle, on arrival somewhere new, or on sustained low ambient.
items.behaviour: Motion is off entirely (`TiqMotion.off`): no draw-in, no cascade, no pulse, no skeleton — and with the count-up now deleted system-wide, Veld and the console finally agree about what motion is for. Loading is the word 'Loading' at 17/600. Press is the inversion to the ink block plus a haptic, which is also the only press cue Veld can afford. Veld costs battery and the product says so, earning it back by shortening the screen-on timeout, dropping GPS to balanced and pausing tile fetches.
items.modes: This IS a mode, single-density by construction; there is no Veld × Console to design.
items.accessibility: Nothing under 9:1 for text or 15:1 for a border. Targets 56. Everything carried by a fill step, a rim or a glow in Night is carried by a 2px border and a word here. At 2.0× on top of Veld's own step-up, body reaches 34px and rows pass 128dp — the layouts absorb it because nothing is pinned.
items.amber: EXACTLY ONE per screen, always the primary commit: a solid `flame600` block with `veld-ink` on it (10.34:1). Burning Flame on white is 1.79:1 and can therefore never be a line, an icon, a border or a word. The nav's active slot is a solid #1B2632 block, so the single amber block is never in competition — and because the nav is exempt chrome in every skin, that rule is now the same rule everywhere rather than a Veld exception.
items.screenshot: A stark white screen with very large near-black type: a big number, one bordered box of figures, three thick-bordered rows of outlets, a docked white nav bar with a 2px black top edge, and a single wide amber block with black text on it — no images, no charts, no grey, no shadows.

openQuestions:
**Resolved by this revision, and no longer open.** (a) The route-dependent nav pill: the active slot is permanently exempt from the ledger, exactly as the focus ring is, because it is persistent chrome and only one slot can be active. Night is now nav block + at most one nominated content amber, which is the two objects the law always claimed. Every substitution rule in the previous draft — the filter chip's, the coverage tick's, the fraud case's dark nav — is deleted. (b) The plate's height: `min(clamp(0.44 × vh, 200, 360), vh − 440)`, with an automatic fall to the 96dp collapsed band under 200, and golden tests at 360×640 / 360×780 / 412×892 × 1.0/2.0 asserting visible decision rows. (c) The fallback-as-default: a tenant whose last thirty plate requests all fell through auto-enables the collapsed band, and the preference ships day one.

**1. Onest versus Archivo.** The brief and `tiq_type.dart` say Onest; `refine-cinematic.json`'s typography section argues for Archivo Variable and declares Inter retired in its favour. I designed to Onest with JetBrains Mono on every figure and identifier, which `TiqTypeToken.family` already enforces via `isFigure`. Someone must delete the losing paragraph. Related and still dead: every `wdth 88–112` instruction in the spec is a no-op, because Onest has no width axis. I specified none.

**2. The nav pill versus the underbar.** Owner decision #3 says a solid amber pill; the spec kills the pill as the most recognisable borrowed gesture in the reference set and substitutes a 3px underbar, citing a 1.4.11 failure at 1.5–2.0:1. I kept the pill, because that contrast objection was against a *translucent* pill: a solid `flame600` block with `onAmber` ink is 10.65:1 for its label and 9.49:1 against the nav body. The plagiarism objection stands and is not mine to answer. If the owner reinstates the underbar, nothing else in this document moves — the underbar and the block are one exempt chrome object either way.

**3. There is still no verdict endpoint.** `fraud_repository.dart` exposes `flagged({minScore})` and nothing else. The verdict control, the 24-hour change window, the "being reviewed by Thabo M." concurrency state and the escalation lock all assume a backend that does not exist. At minimum: `POST /fraud/visits/:id/verdict` carrying reviewer, verdict, reason and timestamp, plus a lock flag the visit detail also honours.

**4. Do Alerts and Tasks stay merged behind one "Work" slot?** They are different objects — a rule firing versus assigned work with an SLA — and the menu lists them separately under OPERATE. Merging keeps the fourth slot for Ask TradeIQ. I chose the merge; both keep their own routes. It is a product call about what a regional manager opens most, and I do not have that data.

**5. The ledger needs a lint, not just an assert.** `TiqLedger` makes the amber law enforceable, but the debug assert only fires on a route someone actually opens in a debug build. The stronger version is a custom analyzer rule: any widget constructed with `lit: true` outside a `TiqLedger.nominate` call is an error. Without it, the law degrades back to prose within a release or two — the same argument that made `semanticLabel` a required constructor argument on the icon button.

**6. The plate's byte cap needs a server owner.** Lossy WebP with alpha at q≈72 under a hard 60 kB cap, baked at two aspect ratios (the phone's fold-budget height and a 21:9 band from 600dp up), with the request deferred behind the decision list. Nobody owns the photos module's encoder settings today, and a 400 kB PNG will reappear the first time someone "improves" the dissolve.

**7. `edgeStructure` is banned on the Day well (2.99:1) and several components rely on it.** The flag chip, the held-work row and the offline banner take `edgeControl` #6E6657 in Day instead. A `TiqSkin.edgeFor(fill)` helper beside the existing `onFill(fill)` would make that unforgettable; without it someone paints an `edgeStructure` outline on a Day well within a month.

**8. What a manager does with a Veld console.** I held the `meta` line saying fraud review is better done sitting down, and I would extend the same line to report results. It is an unusual thing for software to say and it may not survive a product review; the alternative is an escalation recorded in a forecourt at 40% backlight, which I think is worse.

**9. Afrikaans needs a CI gate, not a good intention.** The eyebrow now wraps to two lines at +4% tracking, but the real protection is a pseudo-localisation pass that renders every label at 1.4× its English width and fails on overflow. Without it, the next uppercase tracked label ships untested and clips in Bloemfontein, which is exactly how this one got through.

**10. Three gap tickets still have no console home and I did not invent one.** The decision sheet (#374) and the skip-reason picker (#395) are agent-side; the console reads their output, which I wired into the territory view's unvisited rows. The live outbox row (#391) is agent-side and I built the manager's mirror. If those tickets were meant to produce console surfaces too, this design does not have them.
principles: Darkness is the site, not the style. One gutter line; nothing centred. No cards and no structural dividers — separation is whitespace, mass and rhythm, because a fill or line under 2:1 is invisible on a cheap panel in daylight. Amber is emitted light, never a label: the nav's active slot is exempt chrome, and exactly one content object per screen is lit, nominated by the screen and never defaulted by a component. Severity leaves the amber band entirely. Every figure is tabular mono. An absence is an em dash, a hatch and a sentence — never a zero. The fold is arithmetic with a failing test. Nothing carried by hue alone.
surface: The manager's console — The Floor, alerts, tasks, territories, agent coaching, fraud review with a verdict control, reports, and the first-run board (Torchlight Aisle, Night × Console default, phone first at 360×640dp)
